Special Branch Report No 17
Strike at the Kung Yik Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road
At about 2pm, 4/11/41, a telephone message was received
from Mr Smith, manager of the above Mill, reporting the workers
numbering approximately 1600 males and females, had gone on strike.
D.S.I. Weeks and D.S. Kasukava of the Special Branch
attended and in an interview with Mr Smith learned that on 4/11/41
the workers were given the following increases:-
(a) 30% increase on Basic Pay
(b) 70 cents per day Special Allowance
(c) 2 lbs of rice per pay in lieu of Rice Allowance.
However, when informed of this, the workers refused the above increases
and demanded that they be given:-
(a) 50% increase on Basic Pay
(b) $5.00 per week Special Allowance
(c) 17 lbs of rice per week in lieu of Rice Allowance.
As no settlement could be reached, Police were posted in
the Mill until 6pm when the workers finished their shift.
At 6am, 5/11/41, all workers returned to the Mill, but only
stood by their machines whilst awaiting the result of discussions
between the management and their representatives.
After lengthy discussion, which was attended by Supt Hall,
A/Deputy Commissioner, and members of the Special Branch, the workers
on being informed that the S.M.C. had refused to supply the management
with sufficient rice to enable them to give each worker the 17 lbs they
had demanded, amended their demands and agreed to accept the original

1941年11月4日下午2时许，接到上述纱厂经理史密斯先生（Mr. Smith）的电话留言，报告称该厂约1600名男女工人已举行罢工。
特别处的副督察威克斯（Weeks）和侦探加须川（Kasukava）前往处理，并在与史密斯先生的面谈中获悉，1941年11月4日，厂方给予工人的加薪幅度如下：-
(a) 基本工资增加 30%
(b) 每日特别津贴 70 分
(c) 每次发薪时发放 2 磅大米，以代替米贴。
然而，工人们得知此事后，拒绝接受上述加薪，并要求给予：-
(a) 基本工资增加 50%
(b) 每周特别津贴 5.00 美元
(c) 每周发放 17 磅大米，以代替米贴。
由于未能达成和解，警察被派驻在厂内，直至下午6点工人下班。
1941年11月5日上午6时，所有工人返回工厂，但仅站在机器旁，等待管理层与其代表之间的谈判结果。
经过由代理副警务长霍尔警司（Supt Hall）及特别处成员参与的长时间讨论，当告知工人公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）已拒绝向管理层提供足够的大米，使其无法满足工人每人17磅的要求后，工人修改了他们的要求，并同意接受原先的

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The five arrested mill workers aforedescribed appeared before Judge Wong at the S.S.D. Court on the morning of December 22nd and were placed on writ of Detention until December 29th.

During this period of detention it has been ascertained the five men have not been previously charged.

Enquiries made at the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 160 Robison Road, O.C.L. elicited the fact that although the mill machinery was shut off on December 21st there is no direct evidence against any of the five men in custody to show that they ordered the shutting off of motors. Furthermore, these men admit having, on previous occasions, taken part in conversations among workers regarding the demands, already under consideration by the management, in connection with pay, rice or bonus increases. At these meetings nothing of a criminal nature occurred, therefore in view of insufficient evidence to prefer charges the Court is respectfully requested to cancell the writ of detention and release the five suspects on their appearance on Dec. 29th.

D.D.O."B" Div.

REPORT

Subject Re possible labour trouble at the Hung Yih Cotton Mill, 150
Robison Road.

Made by Det. 21 Smith. Forwarded by V. E. Mason
Officer i/c.

At 10.45 a.m. 9-9-39 the undersigned in company
with C.D.S. 21, visited the Hung Yih (公益) Cotton
Mill, 150 Robison Road, and therein interviewed Mr. Smith
who is the General Manager of the Mill.

Mr. Smith stated that commencing at 6 p.m. 11-9-39
the night shift employed at the above mill cease opera-
tions owing to a shortage of materials.

The night shift is composed of approximately 1,000
female and approximately 500 male workers.

Approximately one third of the male workers now
employed on the night shift will be taken on the strength
of the day shift whilst the remaining males and the
females will not be required for an indefinite period.

Mr. Smith further stated that the night shift
workers have been informed that their work will be
stopped from 6 p.m. 11-9-39 and that it is his opinion
that no trouble with these workers will be experienced.

J.B. Smith

主题 关于罗宾森路150号鸿益纱厂可能发生的劳资纠纷。

由 21号侦探 Smith 制作。由主管官员 V. E. Mason 转呈。

1939年9月9日上午10:45，签署人会同刑事侦缉处21号警员，走访了位于罗宾森路150号的鸿益（公益）纱厂，并会见了该厂总经理 Smith 先生。

Smith 先生表示，自1939年9月11日下午6时起，由于材料短缺，上述纱厂的夜班工人停止作业。

夜班由大约1000名女工和大约500名男工组成。

目前夜班组中约三分之一的男工将转入白班组编制，而其余男工和女工将在无限期内无需上班。

Smith 先生进一步表示，夜班工人已获知他们的工作将从1939年9月11日下午6时起停止，他认为这些工人不会引发麻烦。

J.B. Smith

S.I. Kyla whilst attempting to obtain additional men was called

above decision was postponed. Inspt.i/c and the undersigned
returned to the station.
At 11.25a.m. a telephone message was received at G.R.from

had just rushed inside the Mill.

(51)    Date. May 31st ...... 1937.
Subject Re Changes in Labour System at Kung Yih Mill 150 Robinson Road.

Made by D.S.I. Read.    Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
    A telephone message was received from Mr. Davis (Manager)
at 9.10a.m. 31/5/37 to the effect that all the workers of the
Weaving Department were on strike (in the Weaving Room).
    S.I. Mason, D.S.I. Read with party of Police immediately
attended. D.D.O. "B", D.O. "B" and C.D.I. Ross (S.B.) being
informed by Charge Room Sgt.
    On arrival the actual disturbance had subsided though all
operatives (about 600) of the weaving room were congregated
near the door and were excitedly conversing between themselves
and with the manager (Mr. Davis) and his staff.
    There was evidence of bobbins having been thrown but
little damage was done.
    The workers demand at this time was that they be granted
an allowance of 3 cents per head per day for "rice money"
(an allowance of this nature was previously paid (abolished in
1936) owing to the high price of rice at that time).
    The manager told the workers representatives that he would
give them 15 minutes to decide:-
    1.-To continue working and submit any demands to the management
for consideration or
    2.-To leave the Mill.
    As a riot in the weaving room was possible at any time,
the R.U. was called and "stood by" outside the Mill, on Robinson
Road.
    At about 9.45a.m. Woo Vung Paung (Member of Local Tang-pu)
and Pen You Noong (private assistant of the former and Leader
of 3rd Cotton Weavers Union 7 Ming Sung Li) came in the Mill &
spoke with the workers.

（印：RECEIVED 1 JUNE 1937 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）
（批：It's for Lauby）
（批：S 1/6）

制作人 副督察长（D.S.I.）里德（Read）。    转呈人 [签名]

先生，
    1937年5月31日上午9时10分，接到戴维斯先生（经理）的电话，称织布部所有工人正在罢工（在织布车间内）。
    梅森巡官（S.I. Mason）、副督察长里德（D.S.I. Read）率警队立即到场。值班室警长已通知“B”区副值班官（D.D.O. "B"）、“B”区值班官（D.O. "B"）及特别处的罗斯首席侦探督察（C.D.I. Ross）。
    到达时，实际骚乱已平息，尽管织布车间的所有操作工（约600人）聚集在门口附近，情绪激动地相互交谈，并与经理（戴维斯先生）及其职员交谈。
    有证据显示有人投掷纱管，但造成的损坏很小。
    此时工人的要求是每人每天发放3分钱作为“米贴”（由于当时米价高涨，此前曾发放此类津贴，但于1936年取消）。
    经理告诉工人代表，给他们15分钟时间决定：
    1.- 继续工作，并将任何要求提交管理层考虑，或
    2.- 离开工厂。
    鉴于织布车间随时可能发生暴乱，后备队（R.U.）被召来并在罗宾森路的工厂外“待命”。
    上午9时45分左右，吴云邦（Woo Vung Paung，地方党部成员）和潘有蒙（Pen You Noong，前者私人助理及明松里7号第三棉织工会领袖）进入工厂并与工人谈话。

（印：1937年6月1日收讫 上海公共租界工部局警务处）
（批：给拉比 Lauby）
（批：S 1/6）

Three unsuccessful attempts were made to "resume" work, the
motors were started, but the workers shut off their machines on
each occasion after about 1 minutes running. An Iron bar was
thrown during the third attempt which struck a female worker in
the face causing superficial injury.

As Woo Vung Peang and Pen You Hoong could exercise no
control over the workers, they left the weaving room and Mr.Davis
requested that all the workers, who refused to leave, be ejected
by the Police.

Inspector Koo of 6th Div. was present and requested the
D.O. "B"(Mr. Crouch) to be allowed to call for S.C.G.P.B. Reserve
Unit to effect the ejection of the workers. To this D.O. "B"
agreed at 10.40a.m.

Inspector Koo from that time, by phone and messengers, called
for S.C.G.P.D. Reserve Unit but at 11.50a.m. stated that he could
not obtain any men to attend.

Mr. Davis then requested D.O."B" that the S.M.P. eject these
weaving room workers.

In addition to the above, due to delayed action further
complication was caused by the arrival of food cans from outside
and workers in other departments collecting feed at the gates,
general apprehension of impending "trouble" throughout the Mill
and the fact that the weaving room workers also wanted their
food, but were reluctant to leave the weaving room.

In view of the above the Reserve Unit called for reinforce-
ments and a second squad arrived and stood by on Robinson Road.

No action however was called for and at approx 1.30p.m.
the weaving room workers resumed work on conditions that an answer
be given to their demands within 3 days (same promised by Mr.Davis).

三次尝试“恢复”工作均未成功，电机启动，但每次运行约1分钟后，工人都关闭了机器。在第三次尝试期间，有人投掷了一根铁条，击中一名女工面部，造成轻伤。

由于吴云邦（Woo Vung Peang）和潘有蒙（Pen You Hoong）无法控制工人，他们离开了织布车间，戴维斯先生请求警察驱逐所有拒绝离开的工人。

第六分局的古督察（Inspector Koo）在场，并请“B”区值班官（克罗奇先生 Mr. Crouch）允许呼叫上海市公安局后备队来执行驱逐工人的任务。“B”区值班官于上午10时40分同意了这一请求。

古督察从那时起通过电话和传令兵呼叫上海市公安局后备队，但在上午11时50分表示他无法调集人员到场。

戴维斯先生随后请求“B”区值班官由上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）驱逐这些织布车间工人。

除此之外，由于行动延误，外部食物罐头的送达以及其他部门工人在门口领取食物，导致局势进一步复杂化，全厂普遍担心即将发生“麻烦”，而且织布车间工人也想要他们的食物，但不愿离开织布车间。

鉴于上述情况，被呼叫的后援队请求增援，第二小队抵达并在罗宾森路待命。

然而并未采取实际行动，大约在下午1时30分，织布车间工人恢复工作，条件是必须在3天内对其要求给予答复（戴维斯先生已作出相同承诺）。

Sir,
At 7.35 p.m. 27/5/37 a telephone message was
received from C.D.I.Ross(S.B.) to the effect that a "Tai Kang"
strike was contemplated by workers at the Kung Yih Mill at 8
p.m. 27/5/37.
Precautions were taken by Inspt. 1/o but the strike
did not materialise, the workers representatives having assured
the management at about 8.40 p.m. that there would be no strike.
Enquiries re the cause of present unrest reveals
that a number of weavers who had worked extra hours at the
request of the mill (6 a.m. to 10 p.m.) failed to resume work
at 6 a.m. the following morning. The management took exception
to this, and following a discussion with the workers took on
extra hands.
This caused further unrest amongst the weavers. Terms
of present settlement not yet ascertained.
Later enquiries at the mill a.m. 28/5/37 revealed
that a coolie of the Weaving Dept. named Fung Sung Kwei (方开贵 )
was assaulted at 9.30 p.m. 27/5/37 off Jessfield Road and is at
present detained in the Lester Chinese Hospital. Extent of
injuries not yet known.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(Signature)
D.S.I.
Copy sent to Special Branch.

制作人 副督察长（D.S.I.）里德（Read） 转呈人 (签名)
先生，
1937年5月27日晚上7时35分，接到特别处罗斯首席侦探督察（C.D.I.Ross）的电话，称公益纱厂工人计划于1937年5月27日晚上8时举行“怠工”（Tai Kang）罢工。
主管督察采取了预防措施，但罢工并未发生，工人代表在晚上8时40分左右向管理层保证不会罢工。
关于目前动荡原因的调查显示，一些应工厂要求加班（上午6时至晚上10时）的织布工未在次日早上6时恢复工作。管理层对此表示异议，在与工人讨论后雇佣了额外人手。
这在织布工中引起了进一步的动荡。目前和解条款尚未查明。
1937年5月28日上午在工厂进行的后续调查显示，织布部一名名为方开贵（Fung Sung Kwei）的苦力于1937年5月27日晚上9时30分在杰斯菲尔德路附近遭到袭击，目前留在莱斯特长华医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。受伤程度尚不清楚。
此致，
阁下之恭顺仆人，
(签名)
副督察长（D.S.I.）

Date... May 18th 19 37.
Subject Re Changes in Labour System at King Yih Mill 150 Robinson Road.

Made by D.S.I. Road. Forwarded by (Signature)

Sir,
Payment of compensation to the 60 dismissed workers
was scheduled to commence 9 a.m. 18/5/37. The 60 workers
however did not attend at that hour, but awaited the arrival
of Woo Vung Pong (吳文邦) of City Tang-pu.
At 11.30a.m. they were called to the Mill by Zung Chi
Mo (任積模) of the Bureau of Social Affairs who had attended
as deputy for Wong Ping ( ) of the same Bureau.
On the workers becoming aware that they were not being
paid 3 months wages and any superannuation monies due to them
they refused to accept any money and all congregated outside
the Mill at 12 noon.
Station was informed and Inspector i/c, S.I. Mason and
the undersigned attended, only to learn that the workers had
already moved off in company with Zung Chi Mo (Bureau of Social
Affairs).
Inspector i/c informed C.D.I. Ross Special Branch of
this on his return to the station at 12.25p.m.
Information has later been received that representatives
of these 60 workers are now contacting Bureau of Social Affairs
and City Tang-pu to mediate for a settlement of this question.

(Signature)

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(Signature)
D.S.I.

Copy sent to Special Branch.

由 D.S.I. Road 撰写。转呈人（签名）

先生，
向60名被解雇工人支付赔偿金的工作原定于1937年5月18日上午9时开始。然而，这60名工人并未在该时刻到场，而是等待来自市党部的吴文邦 (Woo Vung Pong) 抵达。
上午11时30分，社会局的任积模 (Zung Chi Mo) 将工人们召至纱厂，他是作为该局黄平 (Wong Ping)（原文此处为空白）的代理出席的。
当工人们得知他们无法获得应付的三个月工资及任何退休金时，他们拒绝接受任何款项，并于中午12时全部聚集在纱厂外。
捕房获悉此事后，负责督察、警佐梅森 (S.I. Mason) 及本报告撰写人随即前往，却得知工人们已随社会局的任积模 (Zung Chi Mo) 离开。
负责督察于下午12时25分返回捕房后，将此情况通报给特别分支的罗斯首席侦探督察 (C.D.I. Ross)。
随后收到消息，这60名工人的代表目前正在与社会局及市党部联系，以调解并解决此问题。

（签名）

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
（签名）
副督察长 (D.S.I.)

副本送特别分支。

Made by.......D.S. Kynstone. Forwarded by (Signature)
Sir,
At about 10p.m. 17/5/37 information was received from
Mr. Davis to the effect that labour trouble was expected in
the Kung Yih Mill, No.150 Robison Road.
In view of the above circumstances Inspt. Hall and the
undersigned immediately proceeded to the Kung Yih Mill where
it was ascertained that trouble was expected because of 4 recently
engaged female overseers, two of whom had had bobbins thrown
at them at about 11a.m. 17/5/37.
Further enquiries however ascertained that Mr. Davis
had severely reprimanded the chief factory labour representative
namely Pao Koh Shing (包国兴) with the result that at about
11.30p.m. 17/5/37 he assured all concerned that there would
be no trouble of any description on the 17th or 18th May 1937.
In view of the above circumstances extra uniform police
have been posted in the factory and C.D.S. 173 has been instructed
to mix with the workers in endeavour to ascertain the definite
cause of the unrest and those responsible.
At the time of writing this report normal working
conditions exist.
Mr. Sinclair D.O."B" informed and Special Branch.
I am, Sir
Your Obedient Servant.
(Signature) D. S. Kynstone
D. S. 182.
(Signatures)
Copy to Special Branch.

先生，
1937年5月17日晚上10时许，收到戴维斯 (Mr. Davis) 先生的消息，称罗宾逊路150号公益纱厂预计会发生劳资纠纷。
鉴于上述情况，霍尔督察 (Inspt. Hall) 及本报告撰写人立即前往公益纱厂，经查明，预计发生骚乱的原因是最近雇佣了4名女性监工，其中两人在1937年5月17日上午11时许被人投掷纱管袭击。
然而，进一步查询查明，戴维斯先生严厉斥责了工厂劳工总代表包国兴 (Pao Koh Shing)，结果是他在1937年5月17日晚上11时30分左右向有关各方保证，1937年5月17日或18日不会发生任何形式的骚乱。
鉴于上述情况，已在工厂增派制服警察驻守，并指令第173号华籍侦探警员 (C.D.S. 173) 混入工人中，试图查明动荡的确切原因及责任人。
在撰写本报告时，工作秩序正常。
已通知“B”区巡官辛克莱尔 (Mr. Sinclair D.O."B") 及特别分支。
先生，
您顺从的仆人。
（签名） D. S. Kynstone
D. S. 182.
（签名）

Made by D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by (Signature)

Sir,

During the day only 51 workers attended for registration
(47 of whom registered during the morning).

Though a medium sized crowd accumulated in the vicinity
of the Mill gates during the morning no incidents took place.
Rumours of registering workers have been stopped and questioned
by other striking workers O.C.L. were received but no confirmation
obtained.

Mr. Davis was interviewed on his return at 5p.m. from a
meeting at Jardine & Mathesons Offices and stated that a full
settlement had been arrived at which had been agreed to by all
the parties concerned.

At about 5.30p.m, two masons actually working at the Mill
were assaulted by a crowd of strikers O.C.L. and were taken to
the 6th Div. kept there for approx 2 hours and then permitted
to leave. Mr. Davis brought these men to Gordon Road Station
at 8.30p.m. and reported the incident.

Mr. Davis then conveyed them to the Lester Hospital where
certificates were issued (in possession of Mr. Davis) which read
as follows:-Ching Sing Foh(金生福) Bruise of left arm and
contusion of chest.

Zing Sih Dau (陳道) Contusion of face & chest.

In view of the fact that a settlement has been arrived at,
registration of workers will continue on 11/5/37 according to the
programme as shown on Report No.40 and it is anticipated that
the Mill will be able to open within about 4 days.

I am, Sir
Your Obedient Servant,
(Signature)
D. S. I.

先生，

当天仅有51名工人前来登记（其中47人是在上午登记的）。

虽然上午在纱厂大门附近聚集了中等规模的人群，但未发生任何事件。收到关于登记工人被其他罢工工人（O.C.L.）拦阻和盘问的谣言，但未获证实。

戴维斯先生下午5时从怡和洋行 (Jardine & Mathesons) 办公室开会回来后接受了问询，他表示已达成全面和解，且所有相关方均已同意。

下午5时30分左右，两名实际上正在纱厂工作的泥瓦匠遭到一群罢工工人（O.C.L.）的袭击，随后被带往第六分区，在那里被扣留约2小时后获准离开。戴维斯先生于晚上8时30分将这些工人带到戈登路捕房并报告了此事件。

随后戴维斯先生将他们送往莱斯特医院 (Lester Hospital)，医院出具了证明（由戴维斯先生持有），内容如下：金生福 (Ching Sing Foh) 左臂挫伤及胸部淤伤。

陈道 (Zing Sih Dau) 面部及胸部淤伤。

Sir,

C.D.S.173 had also heard something to this effect and was detailed to continue enquiry for further information; C.D.S. 173 later reported (at 6p.m.) that it was then proposed for striking workers to enter the Mill compound with workers entering for registration and to create a disturbance inside the Mill compound.
D.J.I. Chu Kang Wei has communicated with Inspector Kyle Ung Chiao ( 贾国兆 ) (6th Div) who was conversant with the situation though he could not definitely say as to the plans of the strikers for the morning of 10/5/37. Sir,

C.D.S.173 reports that at 3 p.m. 7/5/37 about 200
strikers of the Kung Yih Mill congregated at No.7 Ming Sung Li,
Brennan Road. Two representatives attended from the City Tangpu
and addressed the strikers, these representatives being Woo
Veng Pong(吴文邦) and one named Peu(□).

The strikers were advised to resume work as it was
possible that new hands would be taken on if they failed to
do so. However, the strikers intimated that they would not resume.

The meeting broke up at 4.30 p.m. there having been
no incidents.

revealed the following:- Ying Ying Kiu( ) Weaving Depart-
ment shroff(employed for past 9 months)has resided in the mill
compound during the period of the strike and has only left to
make small purchases on Robison Road.
At 7.20 a.m. 29/4/37, he left the mill to
purchase food at a shop on Robison Road about 50 yards distant
from the mill gates.
When returning, and whilst walking in the middle
of Robison Road he was approached by two male Chinese descrip-
tion as follows:-
1st.Height about 5'7"-8",age 25:square face,long
hair,wearing black cotton jacket & pants,Spoke
Fompo dialect.
2nd.Height about 5'6"-7",age 30,wearing black cotton
jacket and pants,round face,hair cut short.
These men accused Ying Ying Kiu of going out to call

two males,assaulted him with their fists.

ran away. C.P.C.s cannot again identify these two men but Ying

desires to proceed against them for Assault. This is now th/

1937年4月29日上午8时55分，接到公益纱厂经理的电话留言，称其一名出纳员在罗宾森路遭到袭击。经督察长里德和督察长朱庚义（Chu Keng ei，音译）立即调查，查明情况如下：应英乔（Ying Ying Kiu，音译），织布部出纳员（受雇过去9个月），在罢工期间一直居住在厂区宿舍内，仅离开去罗宾森路购买少量物品。
1937年4月29日上午7时20分，他离开工厂，前往距离工厂大门约50码的罗宾森路一家商店购买食物。
在返回途中，当他走在罗宾森路中间时，两名中国男子走近他，特征描述如下：
1. 身高约5英尺7-8英寸，年龄25岁：方脸，长发，身穿黑色棉夹克和裤子，讲番禺方言。
2. 身高约5英尺6-7英寸，年龄30岁，身穿黑色棉夹克和裤子，圆脸，短发。
这些人指责应英乔外出召集其他工人进厂工作。他予以否认，上述两名男子用拳头殴打了他。
华籍巡长2920号和2856号观察到路上有骚动，便跑向现场，随后上述两名男子逃跑。华籍巡长无法再次辨认出这两人，但应英乔认出他们是织布部的人，尽管他不知道他们的名字。他能轻易再次辨认出他们，并希望以袭击罪起诉他们。此事现为

(36)    Date. April 28th 1937.
Subject re Changes in Labour System at Kung Yih Mill, 150 Robison Road.
Made by D.S.I. Read.    Forwarded by (Signature)
Sir,
At 5.30p.m. a telephone message was received from the
Kung Yih Mill stating that a large number of striking workmen
were at the rear of the Mill (Chinese Controlled Area). Detectives
attended only to learn that the strikers had already left.
Enquiries were instituted when it was learnt that about
300 male and female strikers had congregated together between
1 abd 3 p.m. on the Chung San Road with the intentions of
proceeding to the City Government. The 6th Division had been
forwarned and it is understood,had received instructions from
City Government to turn these strikers 'back'. This the 6th
Division did and the strikers moved back and at 5.30p.m. passed
the rear of the Kung Yih Mill. The crowd did not stop near
the Mill and no attempt was made to create any incidents.
On reaching Brennan Road the crowd broke up and all went
their respective ways.
In the procession a large number of banners were being
carried on which were Chinese Characters stating
"We want to appeal to Nanking".
C.D.S. 173 has been instructed to keep close observation
for the strikers next move.
I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
(Signature)
D. S. I.
(批：J 1/2 / 29 4)
Copy to Special Branch,

先生，
下午5时30分，接到公益纱厂的电话留言，称大量罢工工人位于纱厂后方（华界区域）。侦探前往查看，仅得知罢工者已经离开。
经查询获悉，约300名男女罢工者于下午1时至3时之间在中山路聚集，意图前往市政府。第六区警察分局已获预先警告，据悉已收到市政府指令将这些罢工者“遣返”。第六区警察分局执行了这一指令，罢工者遂折返，并于下午5时30分经过公益纱厂后方。人群未在纱厂附近停留，也未试图制造任何事端。
到达布伦南路后，人群解散，各自离去。
游行队伍中携带了大量横幅，上面写有中文字样：
“我们要向南京请愿”。
已指示刑事侦缉股第173号探员密切观察罢工者的下一步行动。
此致，
敬礼，

Sir,
At 2p.m. and continuing to 3.30p.m. 27/4/37 a meeting
was held at Tsoong Hyi Wei 7 King Sung Li and was addressed
by Tai Koh Liang who pointed out that it had been learnt
that the Mill contemplated opening up again soon. Tai Koh
Liang told the workers that should the Mill re-open, they

men would be sent to their homes. The above was repeated
by Tai Koh Liang to the workers who came and left during
the above times (about 200 workers attended).
Six females attended at the Mill on 27/4/37 and requested
their pay and the management met their request.

organs. 擁護黨政機關

During the morning of 26/4/37 a notice was posted outside
the tea-shop on Robison Road directly opposite the Kung Yih Mill
translation of which reads as follows:-

Dated 7 April, 26th Year of
Chinese Republic.

"Regarding the disputes between the workers and the
capitalists, they should co-operate for their existence. This
Government and Bureau have repeatedly notified both parties
concerned to this effect.

Recently the disputes between the labourers and capitalists
have been prevalent and have gradually increased in the number
of cases, it is not only detrimental to productions of industry
but also will do harm to the peace and good order of the district
concerned.

During the reconstruction period of our country, the
opinion between the labourers and capitalists should be cooperation
and together uphold each others interests so that the market
will become improved. Although sometimes they have disputes,

1937年4月26日上午，在正对公益纱厂的罗宾森路茶馆外张贴了一则通知，译文如下：

中华民国二十六年四月七日。

“关于劳资纠纷，双方应为生存而合作。本政府及社会局已多次就此通知有关双方。

近期劳资纠纷盛行，案件数量逐渐增加，这不仅不利于工业生产，也会损害相关地区的和平与秩序。

在我国重建时期，劳资双方的意见应是合作，共同维护彼此利益，从而使市场得到改善。虽然有时会有纠纷，

date, all the labour disputes should be referred to this
Government and Bureau for dissolution according to law, and
before the parties concerned have been summoned for settlement
of the dispute, or whilst the matter is in the course of mediation
no strike should be declared by labourers nor the owners close
down their mills. In such a case, this Government and Bureau will
make strict enquiries as to the party who started the trouble
and they will be dealt with severely. If any bad elements attempt
to instigate the strike with a view detrimental to peace and
good order of the social community, they will also be punished
according to law."

"The above notice must be strictly obeyed".

Bureau of Social Affairs.    Signed & Chopped:-

本政府及社会局鉴于这些恶劣行为，已采取措施解决纠纷，以保持社会社区的和平与秩序，并试图改善工业生产状况。有关各方现特别注意，自即日起，所有劳资纠纷均应提交本政府及社会局依法解决，在有关各方被传唤解决纠纷之前，或在调解过程中，劳工不得宣布罢工，业主也不得关闭工厂。在此情况下，本政府及社会局将对挑起事端的一方进行严厉查问，并予以严惩。如有不良分子企图煽动罢工，旨在损害社会社区的和平与秩序，也将依法惩处。”

Sir,

Inspt. i/c and Special Branch informed at 10.35a.m.
C.D.S. 173 was detailed to keep in touch with the situation and to proceed to Cheng-ju if necessary to observe proceedings.
At 4.30p.m. C.D.S. 173 reported that during the afternoon so many of the workers dissented to the plan of going to Cheng-ju that the idea was abandoned.
C.D.S.173 further reported that he had heard a number of the workers during the afternoon of 23/4/37, had proceeded to "Dae Faung Yah Wei"(地方协会) in French Concession though no confirmation of this nor the object of same could be obtained.

Made by D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by (Signature)

Sir,
At 9.30a.m. 22/4/37 C.D.S. 173 supplied the information
that a notice had been posted in No. 7 Ming Sung Li, (Tsoong
Nyi Wei) translation as follows:-
"Notice to all pickets", "Go and beat up 2nd engineer
S Kah Lin". (司惠林) Dated 22nd.
After informing Inspt i/c and D.D.O. "B" the undersigned
first proceeded to the Kung Yih Mill to ascertain who "S Kah
Lin" referred to as same may have referred to a foreigner.
The nearest name to this was that of the No. 1 motorman
"Ling Shu Kwei" which re-arranged could read "Shu Kwei Ling".
The undersigned next proceeded with D.S.I. Chu Meng Wei to
6th Division and interviewed Inspector Chia Iung Zau (賈恩趙)
where the facts were explained to him and together a visit
was made to No.7 Ming Sung Li at about 10.30a.m. No notice
however was in evidence as above reported though from the
condition of the wall it was obvious that numerous notices
had been posted and later taken away.
On again visiting the Mill at 11.15a.m. one named Yuan
King Bei (袁金培) Weaving shroff was present reporting that
at 8.30a.m. 22/4/37 10 or more strikers had gone to his home
O.O.L. and taken him from there to the Tseong Nyi Wei where
he was 'accused' of having started work, it being pointed out
to him that information had been received via Ling Shu Kwei
to that effect.
He satisfactorily explained that he had merely called
at the Mill at 3.30p.m. 20/4/37 to speak with Mr. Zing and was
permitted to go having suffered no injuries or abuse.
Ling Shu Kwei denies having passed any information on

先生：
1937年4月22日上午9时30分，华探目173号提供情报称，在明松里7号（总义会）张贴了一张告示，译文如下：
“致所有纠察队员”，“去殴打二领班 S Kah Lin”（司惠林）。日期为22日。
在向负责督察及“B”区副总监汇报后，卑职首先前往公益纱厂，以查明“S Kah Lin”所指何人，因为该名字可能指代一名外国人。与此名字最接近的是头车工“Ling Shu Kwei”，重新排列后可读作“Shu Kwei Ling”。
随后，卑职与副督察长朱孟伟 (Chu Meng Wei) 一同前往第六巡捕房，会见贾恩赵督察 (Inspector Chia Iung Zau)，向其说明情况，并于上午10时30分左右一同前往明松里7号。然而，现场并未发现上述报告的告示，但从墙壁的状况来看，显然曾张贴过大量告示，随后又被撕去。
上午11时15分再次访问纱厂时，织布间收付员袁金培 (Yuan King Bei) 在场，他报告称，1937年4月22日上午8时30分，十余名罢工工人前往其位于外马路的住所，将他带至总义会，指控他“开始工作”，并指出他是通过凌书贵 (Ling Shu Kwei) 获得此消息的。
他令人满意地解释说，他只是在1937年4月20日下午3时30分到纱厂与郑先生 (Mr. Zing) 谈话，随后获准离开，未受任何伤害或辱骂。
凌书贵否认曾向总义会传递任何信息

Subject Re Changes in Labour System at Kung Yih Mill, 150 Robison Road.
Made by D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by (Signature)
Sir,
A translation has now been made of an official Notice
issued by the Bureau of Social Affairs and posted on the gate
of the Mill alongside that of the management with regard to the
registration of workers;-
Offical Notice No.9705 of The Bureau of Social Affairs,
"A petition has been received from the Kung Yih Cotton Mill,
British concern, to the effect that the mill management have
prepared to re-open the mill, but before doing so, they have
decided to register the striking workers names etc. and a request
was made to this Bureau that an official notice be issued to
inform the workers for their registration in the mill.
It is learnt by this Bureau that owing to the contracting
system of workers in this mill, no registration of workers was
made before and therefore their names, addresses, etc. can not
be located. Now preparations have been made to re-open the mill,
their request for registration of workers is hereby approved and
notice accordingly issued. As regarding the dispute between
workers and the mill, it will be dissolved by this Bureau
according to law.
The workers are therefore notified that the order of this
Bureau for their registration be strictly obeyed!
Signed, Pan Koong Tsen (Chief of the Bureau of Social affairs)
Chopped, Bureau of Social Affairs.
At 9.30a.m. 19/4/37 a number of females attended at the
mill for registration some (about 1/3) were selected and the
remaining 2/3 rejected. Unconfirmed information was received
during the morning that pickets were being formed by the strikers
and that those registering would be assaulted. Further rumour
(批：C1 / 212 / 21.4.)

to the effect that the Japanese intended throwing lime on
registering workers were also at one time current.
6th Div. were communicated with who stated they were
conversant with the situation and were taking precautions.
Following registration, the females were being given slips
of paper with instructions to go to a photographers and have
their photographs taken for record purposes. Information was
however received, that these females were being taken to the
Tsoong Nyi Wei offices where they were being compelled to
surrender these slips. 6th Div. were again notified and stated
they had sent a man to the Tsoong Nyi Wei to stop them doing this.
At about 11.45 a.m. a male Chinese was arrested by S.C.S.Police
just off Robison Road near the Mill (reason not known) he was
taken to Robison Road Sub-station and shortly after transferred
to 6th Div. Station where he was immediately released.
A small crowd had been in the vicinity of the Mill gates
throughout the morning and at about 11.50a.m. these were joined
by a crowd of workers who were carrying the above released male
shoulder high and firing crackers.
At this time an incident appeared imminent and following
receipt of information to this effect Inspt. I/S and the under-
signed immediately attended. On arrival a mixed crowd was in
evidence though there was no commotion as the unruly element
has just previously moved on.
There were about 20 registering females in the Mill who
wished to leave and as it was highly probable that an incident
would "break" on their leaving the Mill the Reserve Unit was
called and stood by whilst the females left at 12.05p.m.
It was very noticeable that on the arrival of the Reserve

称日本人意图向登记工人投掷石灰，也曾一度流传。
已与第六巡捕房联系，他们表示熟悉局势，并正在采取预防措施。
登记结束后，女性们收到纸条，指示她们去照相馆拍照以备记录。然而，接获情报称，这些女性被带往总义会办公室，被迫交出这些纸条。再次通知第六巡捕房，他们表示已派人前往总义会阻止此举。
上午11时45分左右，一名中国男子在纱厂附近的罗宾森路边被上海特别市警察逮捕（原因不明），他被带往罗宾森路分捕房，不久后转送至第六巡捕房，随即获释。
整个上午，纱厂大门附近一直有一小群人聚集，上午11时50分左右，一群工人加入其中，他们将上述获释男子扛在肩上，并燃放鞭炮。
此时，事态似乎一触即发，接到相关情报后，负责督察及卑职立即赶赴现场。到达时，现场可见混杂的人群，但由于闹事分子刚刚离开，并未发生骚乱。
纱厂内约有20名登记的女性希望离开，鉴于她们离厂时极有可能引发事件，后备队奉命待命，女性们于中午12时05分离开。

Date. April 16th 1937.
Subject Re Changes in Labour System at Jung Yih Mill,150 Robison Road.
Made by D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by (Signature)

Sir,
At 9.15a.m. information was received from C.D.S. 173
that a large number of striking workers (about 400) had gathered
at 121 Brennan Road and intended marching to the City Government.
Immediately after receiving this, D.S. Larby (Sp. Br.)phoned the
same information to the undersigned.
Enquiry was immediately instituted to ascertain the
route the striking workers intended to take, and at one time it
was understood they intended to pass along Robison Road in front
of the Jung Yih Mill. Necessary precautions were taken by Inspt.
I/C but at about 11 a.m. it was learnt the party had moved off in
the direction of the Chun San Road.
Enquiry at 6th Div. revealed they were fully conversant
with the situation, and B.W. Station were also notified.
As rain began to fall about 11 a.m. a number of the
workers "fell out" of the parade and it was later learnt that
the remainder were met on the Chun San Road by Inspector Kyia
of 6th Div. and his subordinates who persuaded the striking
workers to break up and return to their homes.
C.D.S. 173 later reported that when the striking
workers moved off from Brennan Road it was their intention to
split into two parties, one to visit the City Government and
the other to visit the Bureau of Social Affairs both parties
to make appeals for the resumption of work. It was also intended
at that time that they remained at the above places until such
time as a satisfactory reply was given.
It is further reported that the prime movers in

呈报人：副督察长里德 (Read)。转呈人：（签名）

先生：
上午9时15分，接华探目173号情报，称大量罢工工人（约400人）聚集在布伦南路121号，意图游行至市政府。
接到此情报后，特别支部的拉比副督察 (D.S. Larby) 立即电话告知卑职相同情报。
立即展开调查，以确定罢工工人拟采取的路线，一度获悉他们打算沿罗宾森路经过荣益纱厂门前。负责督察采取了必要的预防措施，但上午11时左右，获悉该队伍已向春山路方向移动。
向第六巡捕房查询后得知，他们完全了解局势，并已通知百老汇路捕房 (B.W. Station)。
由于上午11时左右开始下雨，部分工人“脱离”了队伍，后来得知，剩余人员在春山路上遇到了第六巡捕房的基亚督察 (Inspector Kyia) 及其下属，他们劝说罢工工人解散并回家。
华探目173号后来报告称，当罢工工人从布伦南路出发时，他们的意图是分成两队，一队前往市政府，另一队前往社会局，两队均要求复工。当时还打算在上述地点停留，直到得到满意的答复为止。
另据报道，此次示威的主要发起人为：-
1. 戴国良 (Tai Keh Liang)

Made by D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by (Signature)
Sir,
The labour manager (Mr. Zing) was interviewed a.m. 15/4/37
on the subject of his appearance in the Nantao Court p.m. 14/4/37
with three others (shown on Report No. 21). He stated that
they were all questioned by the Procurator on questions
relevant to the cause of the present labour trouble, the
disturbance at the mill at 6 a.m. 1/4/37 and their responsibilities
in these matters, after which, they were permitted to leave
at about 4.45p.m.
Approximately 45 fitters and carpenters of the Kong Yih
Mill reported for work on their own initiative a.m. 15/4/37
and were set to work by the management.
At 7 a.m. 15/4/37 a meeting was held at the Tsoong Nyi Wei
and the return to work of the above carpenters and fitters
was discussed. It was later learnt that the Tsoong Nyi Wei
had decided to form a number groups of 10 workers in a group
to assault these fitters and carpenters when they left off
work (5 p.m.).
Special Branch was informed, precautions taken by Inspt.i/c
and 6th Div. P.S.B. were communicated with and requested to
anticipate trouble in the vicinity of the mill under their
control.
No incidents however took place.
I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
(Signature)
D. S. I.
Copy to Special Branch.

阁下，
劳工经理（辛先生 [Mr. Zing]）于1937年4月15日上午接受问询，内容涉及其与其他三人（见第21号报告所示）于1937年4月14日下午出现在南市法院一事。他陈述称，检察官就与当前劳资纠纷起因、1937年4月1日上午6时工厂发生的骚乱以及他们在这些事件中的责任相关的问题对他们进行了讯问，随后他们于下午4时45分左右获准离开。
约45名公益纱厂的钳工和木工于1937年4月15日上午主动报到复工，并被管理层安排工作。
1937年4月15日上午7时，在忠义会（Tsoong Nyi Wei）举行了一次会议，讨论了上述木工和钳工复工一事。后获悉，忠义会决定组建若干个每组10人的工人小组，在这些钳工和木工下班时（下午5时）对他们进行袭击。
已通知特别支部，负责督察采取了预防措施，并与第六区政治保安处取得联系，要求其预判并防范其管辖范围内工厂附近可能发生的麻烦。
然而，并未发生任何事件。
阁下，
您顺从的仆人，
（签名）

Made by D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
The labour manager (Mr. Ting) and 3 others (as shown on Report No. 21) have each received a further summons to appear at the Nantao Court at 1 p.m. 14/4/37. The summons shows "For causing injury". These 4 persons intend to answer to this summons by attending the Court as ordered. Special Branch (D.S. Larby) was informed who stated they would inform Asst. M.A. Mr. Tsien.

A number of workers came to the Mill during the morning of 12/4/37 and requested their pay. The management acceded to this request and about 100 workers were paid during the morning and 20 during the afternoon.

A total of approx. 140 workers have now been paid and the management do not intend paying out any more under present conditions.

Between 9.30 a.m. & 10.30a.m. 13/4/37 about 200 male and female workers held a meeting at Ming Sung Li, Brennan Road. The meeting was address by Lau Lieu (老刘) and the following demands were approved:-

1,- Dismiss Zang Tuh Faung (蔡德芳)
2,- Medical expenses to be paid to the injured workers.
3,- that 9 days wages be demanded from the Mill as strike pay.
4,- Old workers should be promoted to foremen instead of bringing in new foremen.
5,- No workers to be dismissed without reason.

It is also learnt that the "Tseong Nyi Wei" (忠义会) has informed the workers that if the Mill does not re-open after two weeks they will distribute 20 cents per day to each worker.

Sir,
No further incidents have occurred at the Kung Yih
Mill and though prevailed rumours of anticipated trouble on the
5/4/37 and precautions were taken nothing eventuated.
Between 8 a.m. and 9/15 a.m. 5/4/37 a meeting of
the mill workers and representatives of Kung Yih Mill was held
at 121 Brennan Road in the premises of the Kang Koong Primary
School (幹公小學). At the meeting the 8 demands submitted to the
management previously were discussed,besides which the workers
were told not to receive their wages from the mill on 9/4/37
unless the demands were granted. The workers have also been
informed that representatives would be despatched to various
Government organs to lodge requests asking the latters to support
and protect them in dissolving the trouble with the management.
The speaker(name not known) also informed the audience that the
two mills in Yangtsepoo district are supporting them in this
strike both financially and in their movements.

Branch and the D.D.O. "B". I then tried twice at about

on this occasion there was no answer to the room phone. I
then arranged for a Police detail to be at the Mill at 5 a.m.

informed, I have myself informed them by telephone of all
developements since 9 a.m. on the 1st inst.

Sir,
    With reference to the remarks of D.C. (Divisions)
on the report made by D.S. Lockwood re Special Branch not being
informed; It is admitted that this was not done and the
ommission, following the developement of events, is regretted.
It is however submitted in extenuation thereof, that at the time,
the Kung Yih Mill was not the only concern occupying the atten-
tion of the station staff and rumours of trouble in connection
with the Silk Weaving Strike were also prevalent, none of which
had materialised. Through personal contact with Mr. Davis,
the undersigned has been forced to the conclusion that he is
liable to be over apprehensive upon receipt of unfounded rumours
and making allowances for such apprehensiveness, the undersigned
admits that at the time, precautionary measures as taken by
the station (Detectives and Uniforms) appeared ample to meet
the situation.
    This incident has now been carefully noted and
Special Branch will in future be informed in every instance.

先生，
    关于各区副总监（D.C. Divisions）对Lockwood副巡官所作报告中提及未通知特务科一事的批注；承认确实未这样做，鉴于事态的发展，对此疏漏表示遗憾。
    然而，为此提出减轻责任的理由如下：当时，公怡纱厂并非占据分局人员注意力的唯一事项，有关缫丝罢工的骚乱谣言也甚嚣尘上，但这些均未成为现实。通过与Davis先生的个人接触，在下不得不得出结论：他在收到毫无根据的谣言时往往过度担忧；考虑到这种担忧，在下承认，当时分局采取的预防措施（便衣侦探和制服警员）似乎足以应对局势。
    此事现已仔细记录在案，今后在任何情况下均会通知特务科。
    1937年4月2日晚上7时05分，Davis先生致电分局请求援助，称其一名工头被闸北警察逮捕。负责督察和Bynstone副巡官携刑事侦缉处警员173号立即前往公怡纱厂，经查询，获悉以下情况：

然而，为此提出减轻责任的理由如下：当时，公怡纱厂并非占据分局人员注意力的唯一事项，有关缫丝罢工的骚乱谣言也甚嚣尘上，但这些均未成为现实。通过与Davis先生的个人接触，在下不得不得出结论：他在收到毫无根据的谣言时往往过度担忧；考虑到这种担忧，在下承认，当时分局采取的预防措施（便衣侦探和制服警员）似乎足以应对局势。

此事现已仔细记录在案，今后在任何情况下均会通知特务科。

Subject. Changes in Labour System at Kung Yih Mill,150 Robison Road.

Made by D.S.I.Read,    Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
    No further incidents have occurred at the Mill which
is now definitely closed down and the management have decided
to keep the mill closed down for at least one week.
    A notice has been posted on the gate, translation
of which reads as follows:—
    "The bad element amongst the workers who have falsely
represented themselves in order to create a disturbance and
stop the machines without first having obtained permission
from management, has thereby caused a strike in the Kung Yih
Mill. This mill owing to this trouble, now has to be closed
down by this firm. It has been decided that beginning from
9 a.m. 9/4/37, the workers wages which have been deposited in
the mill will be paid. Signed. The Two Company".
    It is learnt that a meeting was held at 7 Ming
Sun Li (Tsoong Nyi wei) at between 1 and 2 p.m. 1/4/37 when
it was decided to hold another meeting at the same place
8 a.m. 2/4/37, for the purpose of selecting representatives
to proceed to the City Government.
    Chow Oong Kyi (□□□) of Tsoong Nyi Wei is a prime
mover in this present unrest.
    It is known that Special Branch have their detec-
tives and agents covering these meetings and C.D.S 299 has been
detailed to attend the meeting at 8 a.m. 2/4/37.

                                        I am, Sir,
                                    Your obedient servant,
                                        [Signature]
                                        D.S.I.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Attempt made by Kung Yih Mill employees to induce the Ewo & Yangtsepoo Mill workers to go on sympathetic strike.

About 1 p.m. 1-4-37 2 motor hire cars carrying about 12 persons drew up at the Ewo Mill Yangtzepoo Road and the passengers requested to be allowed to enter. It was ascertained by the watchman that the passengers were Kung Yih Mill Workers from Robinson Road as they requested permission to interview the Ewo Mill employees, they were refused admittance and left.

At 5.30 p.m. 1-4-37, as a result of the clash between Police and workers at the "Kung Yih" Cotton Mill Robinson Road 1-4-37 a.m., about 200 of the Kung Yih employees gathered at Thorburn and Chaulpo Roads extensions O.O.L. for the purpose of meeting the "Ewo Mill" and "Yangtzepoo" Mill workers proceeding to the mills for night shift. The Kung Yih workers attempted to get the workers to go on a sympathetic strike and explained how many workers had been injured in the clash with the Police. The workers of the Ewo and Yangtzepoo Mills refused to go on strike and proceeded to work.

Sir,
At 8 p.m. 31/3/37, Mr. Davis of the Kong Yih Mill
telephoned to the station and passed the information that he
had heard trouble was contemplated by the workers during the
changing of shifts A.M. 1/4/37.
Detectives and uniform parties were posted.
During the changing of shifts, (at 5.45 a.m.,)
trouble arose throughout the mill resulting in shouting and
bobbin throwing, and on the seriousness of the situation being
realised the Reserve Unit was turned out, attended and operated,
and by approximately 7.45 a.m. the mill was cleared of workers.
At about 7.45 a.m. the Russian Regiment S.V.C.
attended but their active services were not required and they
merely stood by outside the mill on Robison Road.
Enquiries reveals that at the time the trouble
started approximately 3,000 workers (day & night shifts) were in
the various departments of the mill. It cannot be ascertained
in what department the trouble first broke out and it would
appear from enquiries that it had been arranged for a fixed
time and so occurred simultaneously in all departments.
Damage has not yet been estimated but at present
it is believed to be confined to damaged bobbins and a few
broken windows.
It is known that the Tsoong Yee Wei (忠義會)
have since the resumption of normal working been trying to get
the management to accept their demands--mainly same as those
shown on Report No.11.
It has now been learnt that at 2.15 p.m. 31/3/37
Mr. Wong Tsah Tsang of Bureau of Social Affairs called on the

已部署探员及制服警员驻守。
在换班期间（上午5时45分），全厂范围内发生骚乱，导致叫喊和投掷纱管，鉴于事态严重，后备队出动、到场并展开行动，至上午7时45分左右，工厂内的工人已被清空。
上午7时45分左右，俄国志愿队（S.V.C.）到场，但无需其采取实际行动，他们仅在罗宾森路厂外待命。

损失尚未估算，但目前认为仅限于损坏的纱管和几扇破碎的窗户。
据悉，自恢复正常工作以来，忠义会一直试图让资方接受他们的要求——主要与第11号报告中列出的要求相同。

File No. 7693
Misc.No.23/37. Gordon Road Station,
REPORT(14) Date February 26th 1937.

Subject Contemplated Changes in Labour System at Kung Yih Mill,
150 Robison Road.

Made by D.S.I. Read. Forwarded by

Sir,

The Mill continued to operate throughout the day shift
with only approx. 10% of workers (just over 300).

Some of the returned workers who, during the strike, had
been acting in concert with the "Tsoong Yee Wei" revealed that
pickets had been posted by the "Tsoong Yee Wei" at the points
shown below and that in all probability these pickets would
be continued.

1.- Connaught Road and Singapore Road Corner.
2.- Brenan Road Edinburgh Road Corner.
3.- Robison Road in front of Edison Works.
4.- Zau Kah Doo Bridge.
5.- Jessfield Road Kinnear Road Corner.

This information was passed to Inspt. i/c who, it is under-
stood, with the co-operation of B. W. covered points, 1, 2, 3,
and 5. In addition to this a Gordon Road detective was detailed
for each point (including Zau Kah Doo Bridge for observation only).

At about 4p.m. 26/2/37, Mr. Davis telephoned to the under-
signed to the effect that members of the "Tsoong Yee Wei" had
openly posted a notice-on top of the Kung Yih Mill Notice- on
the gates of the Mill. Mr. Davis at this time was rather
indignant that this had been done under the eyes of Police posted
at the gate to guard against any such incidents.

Enquiry on this point revealed that at the time the notice
was posted, a foreign employee and two clerks of the Mill were
standing at the gate and as they took no notice of the incident
and the notice itself read favourably to the Mill, the two C.P.C.s
were under the impression that everything was "in order".

Within a short time the notice was taken down by Mr.Davis,

由 高级探员 阅毕。转呈

阁下，

工厂在白班期间继续运营，仅有约10%的工人（刚超过300人）。

一些在罢工期间与“忠义会”协同行动的返岗工人透露，“忠义会”已在下列地点部署了纠察队，并且很可能将继续维持这些纠察队。

1.- 康纳特路（Connaught Road）与新加坡路（Singapore Road）转角。
2.- 布伦南路（Brenan Road）与爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）转角。
3.- 爱迪生电气公司前的罗宾森路。
4.- 曹家渡桥。
5.- 极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）与金尼尔路（Kinnear Road）转角。

此信息已传递给负责督察，据悉，他在工务局（B. W.）的配合下覆盖了第1、2、3和5点。此外，每个点都指派了一名戈登路探员（包括仅用于观察的曹家渡桥）。

1937年2月26日下午4时许，戴维斯先生致电卑职，称“忠义会”成员公然在工厂大门上张贴了一份通知——覆盖在公益纱厂原有通知之上。戴维斯先生当时对此感到相当愤慨，因为这是在驻守大门以防此类事件的警察眼皮底下进行的。

对此事的调查显示，在张贴通知时，一名外籍员工和两名工厂职员正站在门口，由于他们未对该事件予以注意，且通知内容本身对工厂有利，两名中国便衣警探（C.P.C.s）误以为一切“正常”。

不久后，戴维斯先生撤下了该通知，

（印章：LIABLE 1 MAR 1937）

Sir,

No attempt was made to open the Mill during the
day, 24/2/37.

At 6.30 p.m. 24/2/37 Mr. Davis received intimation
from his Head Office that the dispute had been settled as far
as negotiating with Bureau of Social Affair and Labour Union
Leaders and that an attempt was to be made to open the Mill
for the day shift 25/2/37 (5.30 a.m.)

At 5 a.m. 25/2/37, a notice chopped by the Head
of the Bureau of Social Affair was posted outside the Mill.
Translation as follows:-

"The cancellation of the contracting system in
the Kung Yih Cotton Mill of the British combine, it is for the
benefit of workers and not to their disadvantage.

"The settlement has now been reached between the
two parties and the workers should cause no further trouble.
Recently the workers have been instigated by the bad elements
and suddenly declared a strike".

"The unreasonable demands made to the management
show that the strike is detrimental to Peace and good order.
Members have repeatedly been despatched by this Bureau and the
Kuomintang Party to give advice to the workers. The majority
of workers have now realised that this strike is to no purpose
but a few of the bad elements are still instigating their fellow
workers and are preventing the willing workers from working".

"This is against the law and an investigation will be made by
this Bureau of their movements and the leaders actions. They
will be arrested and severely dealt with".

"This notice is to all the workers of the mill that

Sir,
Between 7 a.m. & 8 a.m. 25-2-37 a number of pamphlets similar
to the attached, which when translated reads as follows:-
" Fellowmen of the Ewo Cotton Mill! We declare strike for
the sole purpose of struggling for existence. Down with our
traitors Pang Zung Poo (潘隆波), Pang Lau Zee (潘老铨) and
Tai Tuh Fong (泰德芳). They are no good to us. On several
occasions, they sent for loafers to assault our fellowmen.
They are managers' running dogs; They have caused 3 or 4
of our fellowmen to be dismissed by our employers. By doing
so, they can employ their own men to take places of our
fellowmen. Now our fellowmen. Wake up and go on strike
against our traitors and their fellowmen. We must work
together, and protect our fellowmen from being dismissed.
By doing so, we have to send our representatives to the
Jardine Matheson & Company to hand in our petition. Fellowmen
make haste with this matter.
Workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mills
24-2-37."
were found to have been dropped on the premises of the Ewo Cotton
Mill 670 Yangtzepoo Road.
Enquiries were made by C.D.S.'s 98 and 104 but the person
responsible for the dropping of the pamphlets was not traced. As
will be seen from the translation the pamphlet requests the work-
ers of the Ewo Cotton Mill to go on strike in sympathy with the
workers of the "Kung Yih" Cotton Mill, Jessfield Road.
Precautions have been taken by detectives being posted in the
vicinity of the Ewo Mill when the Mill changes shifts, for the
purpose of preventing any intimidation or pamphlet distribution.

阁下：
1937 年 2 月 25 日上午 7 时至 8 时之间，发现若干与附件相似的小册子散落在杨树浦路 670 号怡和纱厂厂区内，其译文如下：
“怡和纱厂的同胞们！我们宣布罢工，唯一目的是为生存而斗争。打倒我们的叛徒潘隆波（Pang Zung Poo）、潘老铨（Pang Lau Zee）和泰德芳（Tai Tuh Fong）。他们对我们没有好处。他们多次叫来流氓殴打我们的同胞。他们是经理的走狗；他们导致雇主解雇了我们三四名同胞。通过这样做，他们可以雇佣自己的人来取代我们的同胞。现在，我们的同胞们。醒醒吧，对我们的叛徒及其同伙进行罢工。我们必须团结起来，保护我们的同胞不被解雇。为此，我们必须派遣代表前往怡和洋行递交请愿书。同胞们，赶快行动吧。
公益纱厂工人
1937 年 2 月 24 日。”
经刑事侦缉处第 98 号和第 104 号探员查询，未能追踪到投放传单的责任人。从译文可以看出，该传单要求怡和纱厂工人罢工，以声援极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）“公益”纱厂的工人。
为防止任何恐吓或传单分发行为，已在怡和纱厂换班期间部署侦探在附近采取预防措施。

J.L. 26/2

Fellowmen of the Kwo Cotton Mill! We declare strike for the
sole purpose of struggling for existence. Down with our traitors
Fang Lung Foo (潘隆波), Pang Lau See (潘老錫) and Tai Tuh Fong
(戴篤芳). They are no good to us. On several occasions, they
sent for loafers to assault our fellowmen. They are managers' running
dogs! They have caused 3 or 4 of our fellowmen to be dismissed by our

our fellowmen from being dismissed. By doing so, we have to send
our representatives to the Jardine Matheson & Company to hand in our
petition. Fellowmen! make haste with this matter!

Workers of the Kung Yih Cotton
Mills.           24/2/37.

(residing 17/47 Chengtu Road) who attended in the capacity of
interpretation.
The six demands are as follows:-
(1) Demand that the nine No. 1 men who have been retired to be
paid their compensation and their superannuation fund all
at once in a lump sum.
(2) Demand that all those discharged workers to be allowed to
return to work. If this demand cannot be granted that these

as a legal organisation. All this clubs expenses are to be
paid by the Mill. This club however guarantees that the

and that there shall no more strike.

截至1937年2月20日，虽经理在办公室留守至晚上9点20分，但仍未收到厂方对工人六项要求的答复。
2月21日上午从侦探处获悉，工人代表将于1937年2月21日下午1点左右在康纳路（Connaught Road）附近举行会议。经进一步查询，确定地点为康纳路旁高生福（Kau Sung Foh）和陆嘉仔（Kau Chia Tsa，音译）的住所。
出席者包括七名退休领班（见第6号报告所列）以及以下人员：姚祥（Yau Ziang）、陸高夫（Lau Kao Foo）和胡铁三（Hoo Tai San）。
会议的具体过程尚不清楚，但通过高生福和社会局代表（曾先生）的传达，得知结果如下，厂方已进一步让步：
对于最初获赔4.00元、后（见第9号报告）增至5.00元和6.00元的被解雇童工，厂方现向所有这些童工提供8.00元。
对于落纱苦力，原提供一个月的工资作为补偿，后增加至两个月（见第9号报告），厂方现提供两个半月的工资作为补偿。
给予摇纱出纳员三个月的补偿。
厂方男工目前似乎感到满意，尽管代表们并未就此作出明确表态。明确表示不满的是四名一级女工，她们表示不会在这些条件下复工，尽管厂方努力联系她们进行讨论但未果。

Sir,
After consultation at the Head Office the following
reply to the workers demands has been formulated by the manage-
ment:-
The Mill
1. Cannot agree to pay 4 months salary as compensation
together with superannuation fund at once. On the
contrary, since the No.1 men have broken faith with
the mill in that they have been engaging in harmful
activities directed against the mill, they have,
strictly speaking, forfeited their superannuation
fund, but in view of their long service, the mill is
prepared to grant 4 months salary as compensation
payable at the end of one month, provided that during
that period the mill has been running with a full
complement of workers in all departments. The mill
at the end of six months will be prepared to pay the
superannuation fund.
2. Cannot agree.
3. The mill is prepared to grant the 14 winding down

Sir,

A.M. 19/2/37 the representative of Bureau of Social
Affairs (Mr. Tsang Tso Jong) met the following seven representa-
tives of the workers in the home of the first named at 68
Brennan Road:

1. Wei Dau Kung (魏道根).
2. Loh Foh Sung (陸福生) all foremen who were paid
3. Ying Kung Sing (邢根生) off on change of scheme
(shown on Report No.6)
4. Yang Ai Ziang (楊愛祥)
5. Voo Tseng San (武增三)
6. Tung Lien Fah (董連發)
7. Peu Ching Yun, (潘清雲)
alias Pai Ah Ching(白阿青).

During this meeting the following demands were
presented by them:-

1. The foremen who have been retired demand immediate
payment of the 4 months compensation and full superannuation in
a lump sum.

Note. (It will be recalled that the offer of the management
was 4 months wages to be paid monthly and full
superannuation to be paid after 6 months had expired,
all to be conditional on no trouble being experienced
in the Mill in respect of this change over).

2. All workers dismissed after February 8th,1937 to be
re-instated.

3. To those workers who cannot be re-instated payment
of 10 months compensation be made.

4. No more workers to be dismissed.

5. Cancel the new appointments made under the new scheme.

Sir,

As no No.1 & 2 women and 174 workers of Spinning
Dept. attended for work, day shift 5.30 a.m. 18/2/37 the Spinnin
Dept. was unable to continue working with the 126 workers who
did attend. The spinning Dept. has therefore been closed down
for the day.

This will cause a stoppage later in the day in the
inding and Reeling Depts. owing to shortage of yarn, (about 10 s
). The weaving Dept it is expected, will continue working through
out the day.

No demands have yet been made and the reason for
this sudden stoppage is believed to be due to agitators operat-
ing amongst and intimidating the workers O.O.L. and whilst
on their way to work O.O.L.

C.D.S.173 and C.D.C.242 have been detailed to
make enquiries amongst the workers in an effort to find who
is behind this latest move.

The following are the 7 foremen who were paid
off during the New Year:-
(1) Tung Lien Wah (童連發), Foreman.
(2) Loh Foh Sung (陸福生), "

(6) Pen Ching Yun (潘錦文), " " "
(7) Voo Tsung Sam (符珍三), Weaving Sub-Contractor:
Winding Dept.

I am, Sir,

先生：

由于1号和2号女工以及纺纱部的174名工人未于1937年2月18日上午5时30分的白班出勤，纺纱部无法仅凭到场的126名工人继续运作。因此，纺纱部当日停工。

这将导致稍后络纱部和缫丝部因缺纱（约10支纱）而停工。预计织布部将全天继续工作。

目前尚未提出任何要求，此次突然停工的原因据信是由于煽动者在工人上下班途中（O.O.L.）进行活动并恐吓工人所致。

已指派 C.D.S.173 和 C.D.C.242 在工人中进行调查，以查明此次最新行动背后的主使者。

Sir,

In compliance with instructions of D.O."B" the
undersigned interviewed Mr. Davis, Manager of Kong Yih Mill
at 9.30 a.m. 6/2/37 on the matter the subject of this report.
From past contacts with this mill and from information revealed
during the above interview the position can be set out as under:
In October 1935 the two mill labour contractors were
arrested(on behalf of P.S.B.) by J.R., and after lengthy legal
arguments were handed over to the Procurator of Shanghai
District Court to be held pending investigations into murder
charges. They were later both charged with murder, and it is
believed that they were convicted and sentenced to 15 years
imprisonment each(.See G.R.Misc. No.107/35).
From October 1935 the son of one of the above labour
contractors was permitted to deputise for the above two under
arrest and continued to be so employed in the capacity of Labour
Contractor until the later part of 1936, by which time, the
management had realised that this arrangements was unsatisfactory.
In view of this, a change was made and Mr. Zing Tuh Fong was
given the position of Labour Contractor.
This change(Mr. Zing Tuh Fong is a foreign trained
student) caused apprehension amongst the workers, mainly amongst
No.1 Foremen, who saw the possibility of changes being made to their
disadvantage. Some unrest existed for a time, but subsided,
following a promise made by the new Labour Contractor Mr. Zing
Tuh Fong to the effect that he would not make radical changes
and would not dismiss the old No.1s and substitute others of
his own selection.(Gordon Road Miss. No. Political 18/34 refers)
The system in the past has been the usual one of

先生，

遵照“B”区巡官（D.O."B"）的指示，签署人于1937年2月6日上午9时30分会见了公义纱厂经理戴维斯先生，讨论本报告所述事项。根据以往与该工厂的接触以及上述会谈中披露的信息，情况可陈述如下：
1935年10月，两名工厂劳工包工头被 J.R. 逮捕（代表警务处特别支部 P.S.B.），经过漫长的法律辩论后，被移交给上海地方法院检察官羁押，以待谋杀罪指控的调查。后来两人均被控谋杀，据信他们被判有罪，各判处15年监禁。（参见 G.R.杂项号 107/35）。
自1935年10月起，上述一名劳工包工头的儿子获准代替上述两名被捕者行事，并以劳工包工头的身份继续受雇，直至1936年下半年，此时管理层已意识到这种安排令人不满。
鉴于此，进行了变更，郑土芳（Zing Tuh Fong，音译）先生被任命为劳工包工头。
这一变更（郑土芳先生是一名受过外国教育的学生）在工人中引起了担忧，主要在1号工头中，他们看到了可能做出对其不利的变更。曾出现过一段时间的不安，但随着新任劳工包工头郑土芳先生承诺不会进行激进变革，也不会解雇旧的1号工头并替换为他自行挑选的人，不安情绪得以平息。（参见戈登路杂项号 政治 18/34）

contractor, sub-contractor and sub-contractors, with sub-contractors responsible for taking on workers. Payment of wages has been from office to Labour Contractor, who then pays his sub-contractors who in turn passes the payments on.
This system is definitely detrimental to the workers, and to the management in that there are numerous persons not actually engaged on production who are getting appreciable profits from their respective positions.
The now proposed changes are being made in an effort to re-organise the whole system and to bring each worker directly under the management for appointment, pay and control.
(批：At a fixed salary // of)
The management are proposing to cancel the labour contract with Mr. Zing Tuh Fong but will offer him the position of labour manager. (He has not yet been told of this, and his acceptance is therefore at present uncertain).
A system has been worked out to bring all workers under control of the office and this will necessitate the dismissal of 8 to 15 No.1 foremen or sub-contractors (exact number not yet known). It will be noted that these are the men who received promises of continued employment from the labour contractor but of course, the matter has now been taken of his hands by the Head Office.
The changes will also involve the dismissal of about 200 small boys who have been employed in moving bobbins from spindles etc. It would therefore appear that in addition to these dismissals, the workers will have to continue without the assistance of these boys and may therefore have cause for dissatisfaction on that score.

C.D.C. 16 during the changing of shifts and none other than

Discreet enquiries amongst the workers have failed
to reveal anything of interest and it would appear, that the

The situation is normal and observation and enquiries

There is no definite unrest at the present time amongst workers. Mr. Davis has conferred with all the foremen and asked them to state any dissatisfaction which may exist. Nothing however was brought to light and all stated conditions were satisfactory and no unrest existed.
There is however a rumour afoot that efforts are being made to organise a union but no confirmation of this has been obtained.
There is also a rumour afoot that a strike will be declared in the near future.
Although no demands have been made the management are granting an increase in wages of 5% effective from 27/12/36 and notices to this effect have been posted. This is being done in view of the fact that 5% increase have been granted in other mills recently and that the voluntary increasing of wages by the management may avert further trouble.
A little apprehension has been shown by the workers for the past month since Mr. Ting Tuh Fong(秦德芳) has taken over the position as labour contractor, but as no changes in staff have been effected and Mr. Ting Tuh Fong has given assurances that none is intended, this apprehension has greatly diminished.
It will be recalled that the previous contractors Zau Tseng Zee(趙春泉) and Zau Ping Zee(趙炳泉) were arrested on 1/10/35 at the request of P.S.B. on charges of Murder(August 1928) and were later, after much legal argument, handed over to the Procurator of Shanghai District Court on 1/11/35 (Gordon Rd.Misc.No.107/35 refers)
These two men are believed to be serving sentences

目前工人中没有明确的骚乱迹象。Davis 先生已与所有领班会谈，并要求他们陈述任何可能存在的不满情绪。然而，并未发现任何问题，所有人都表示状况令人满意，不存在骚乱。
但是，有谣言称正在努力组织工会，但尚未获得证实。
另有谣言称，近期将宣布罢工。
虽然尚未提出任何要求，但管理层决定自1936年12月27日起加薪5%，并已张贴告示。此举是考虑到最近其他工厂也给予了5%的加薪，且管理层主动加薪可能会避免进一步的麻烦。
自从 Ting Tuh Fong（秦德芳）接任劳工承包商一职以来，过去一个月工人们表现出些许担忧，但由于人员并未变动，且 Ting Tuh Fong 先生保证无意变动，这种担忧已大大减轻。
回想起来，前任承包商 Zau Tseng Zee（趙春泉）和 Zau Ping Zee（趙炳泉）应特别支部请求，于1935年10月1日以谋杀罪（1928年8月）被捕，经过大量法律辩论后，于1935年11月1日被移交给上海地方法院检察官（参见戈登路杂项档案第107/35号）

Enquiries by D.S. Ware and C.D.S. 142.

At 8.15p.m. 11/11/37 Major K.M. Bourne D.C.
(Special Branch) telephoned Bubbling Well Station
and ordered the undersigned to make enquiries concern-
ing a mob assault on Brenan Road at about 6.45p.m.
which involved Mr. T.F. Zing (秦德芳) Chinese
Staff Manager of the Kung Yik Cotton Mill, 150
Robison Road, and some dismissed employees.

Prior to the above report, C.D.S. 142 had been
making preliminary enquiries concerning an assault
case reported by St. Luke's Hospital, Avenue Haig.
At 8.20p.m. he brought to the station Mr. T.F. Zing
and his two unarmed bodyguards Yoen Sung An (袁松岩)
and Pei Mow Lien (白茂連). Yoen Sung An was
treated at the hospital for scalp injuries.

Mr. Zing (秦德芳) gave the following outline
of events leading up to the assault:-

During April 1937 a strike occurred at the Kung
Yik Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, subsequent to the
suspension of contract labour in favour of direct
employment through Mr. Zing the Chinese Staff Manager.
As a result of the strike about 60 employees were
dismissed during May. The majority dismissed (about
40) received full superannuation benefits while the
remainder received a gratuity of three months pay.
Among those receiving superannuation benefits were
four men who were prominent during the strike, namely
Yih Tsung Foo (葉增福), Kyau Ching Kung (喬金根),
Zien Ah S (徐阿四) and Wu Ching Nyoen (吳金源).
The results appeared to be satisfactory to both

1937年11月11日晚8时15分，特别处副督察 K.M. Bourne 少校致电静安寺捕房，命令下文签署人就当晚约6时45分在布伦路（Brenan Road）发生的一起群殴事件进行调查，该事件涉及罗宾森路150号公益纱厂（Kung Yik Cotton Mill）华籍职员经理秦德芳（Mr. T.F. Zing）先生及部分被解雇员工。

在上述报告之前，刑事侦缉处第142号已就海格路圣卢克医院报告的一起袭击案进行初步调查。晚8时20分，他将秦德芳（Mr. T.F. Zing）先生及其两名未携带武器的保镖袁松岩（Yoen Sung An）和白茂連（Pei Mow Lien）带至捕房。袁松岩因头皮受伤在医院接受治疗。

As Mr. Zing attempted to walk away from the mob, the latter shouted "ta" (strike) and roughly dragged the former to a piece of waste land by the P.W.D. sewage sump. When the two bodyguards Yoen Sung An (袁松安) and Pei How Lien (白茂連) attempted to rescue their master, one of the mob shouted "take your weapons" (i.e. nau ka-sang)(拿傢伙). Sticks were then used freely on the bodies of Mr. Zing and his bodyguards.

A few moments later, Mr. Zing broke free from the crowd and ran back toward Brenan Riees for police assistance. On the way he met Mr. Broadman (also employed by the Kung Yik) and by the time he had explained what had happened, the fight was over.

After Mr. Zing's get-away, the bodyguard Yoen Sung An was holding the mob leader Yih Tsung Foo, but was compelled to relinquish his grip when one of the mob struck him on the back of the head with a small axe. Yoen Sung An turned and grasped his assailant who was later arrested by a S.C.G.P.B. officer and taken to Zau Ka Doo Station. However, the axe was not found.

In requesting for your assistance to uphold justice
and to "help" the arrested workers, we, Zung Shing Man
(張生漢), Pan Kuh Shing(潘克鑫) and Wong Ah Nyi(王阿二),
representatives of the workers of the Kung Yik Cotton Mill,
British concern, at Jessfield, beg respectfully to lay before
you the following facts:-

Owing to the continual increase in the cost of living
and the difficulty of maintaining a livelihood with our
scanty wages, we, workers of the above mentioned mill, went
on strike in April of this year following the refusal of
the management to consider our demand for an increase in
wages. Subsequently we resumed work on the conclusion
of an agreement between the employer and the employed, which
was effected through the mediation of the local Tangpu, the
Bureau of Social Affairs and other official organs. The
terms of the agreement were as follows:-
(1) The issue of a rice allowance of 3 cents each per day.
(2) The issue of a bonus equal to one day's wages in every
two weeks' time.
(3) The issue of a food allowance of 2 cents each to those
employed on the night shift.
(4) No workers to be dismissed without reasonable
cause.

As the management failed to observe the agreement,
we, the petitioners, appointed by our fellow workers as their
representatives, interviewed Mr. Davies, the manager, and
Mr. Sing Tuh Peng, the Chinese manager, at 9 a.m. May 31,
and requested them to enforce the agreement without further
delay They promised to give us a reply on June 2, Thursday

However, the management had the evil intention of
upsetting the agreement and started to make trouble with the
workers. On June 2, when the workers had entered the
factory, the management suddenly reduced the wage of one
named Sung Ching Hai, a female worker of the spinning
department, from 50 cents to 40

在请求阁下主持公道并“帮助”被捕工人之际，我们，张生汉、潘克鑫和王阿二，系位于极司菲尔路的英商公益纱厂工人代表，谨恭敬地向阁下陈述以下事实：-

由于生活成本不断上涨，且微薄的工资难以维持生计，我们上述纱厂的工人于今年四月因资方拒绝考虑我们增加工资的要求而举行罢工。随后，在当地塘浦办事处、社会局及其他官方机构的调解下，劳资双方达成协议，我们遂复工。协议条款如下：-
(1) 每日发放每人3分的大米津贴。
(2) 每两周发放相当于一天工资的奖金。
(3) 向夜班工人每人发放2分的伙食津贴。
(4) 若无正当理由，不得解雇任何工人。

由于资方未能遵守协议，我们请愿人作为工友推选的代表，于5月31日上午9时会见了经理戴维斯先生和华方经理辛笃彭先生，要求他们立即执行协议。他们承诺于6月2日星期四给予答复。

然而，资方怀有破坏协议的恶意，并开始找工人麻烦。6月2日，当工人进入工厂后，资方突然将纺纱部一名名叫宋清海的女工的工资从50分降至40

and affects her livelihood, the female worker applied
to foreman Tsui for restoration of the original
number of spindles. Instead of getting satisfaction,
she was dismissed. Another female worker named
Tsang Ying Dah, in the same room, was annoyed, as,
according to the agreement, no workers could be
dismissed without reasonable cause, and she consequently
argued with the foreman. The foreman, however,
deliberately found fault with Tsang and assaulted and
injured her with his fists. This aroused the indignation
of all the other female workers who demanded him to
give an explanation of his violence. In a short while,
the foreman Tsui called in a large number of Chinese and
foreign detectives and policemen, who had been hiding
on the factory premises. Without enquiring into the
cause, the police summarily arrested all the operatives -
10 females and 4 males. This was evidently a
premeditated plot of the management who intended to
break the agreement by finding fault with the workers.
The workers were then surprised and, through the
persuasion of the petitioners, they continued operations
until the time to cease work.
When the night shift workers came to work and
learned of the incident, they, for the sake of justice,
requested the management to effect the release of the
arrested workers. However, when they had hardly
completed their statement, policemen and detectives
rushed in and arrested five workers without having
first enquired into the case. The other workers were
so afraid that they feared to utter a single word.
On the following day, June 4, a female worker
named Tsang Ah Mei (張阿妹) was arrested.

分，这影响了她的生计，该女工向崔领班申请恢复原来的锭数。她非但未获满意解决，反而被解雇。同车间的另一名女工张英达对此感到愤怒，因为根据协议，若无正当理由不得解雇工人，因此她与领班发生争执。然而，崔领班故意挑剔张的毛病，并用拳头殴打致伤。这激起了其他所有女工的愤慨，她们要求他对暴力行为作出解释。不久，崔领班召来了大量潜伏在厂区内的中外侦探和警察。警方未调查原因，便仓促逮捕了所有操作工——10名女性和4名男性。这显然是资方蓄意策划的阴谋，意图通过挑剔工人来破坏协议。工人们当时感到震惊，但在请愿人的劝说下，他们继续工作直至下班时间。
当夜班工人来上班并得知此事后，出于正义感，他们要求资方释放被捕工人。然而，当他们尚未陈述完毕时，警察和侦探冲入现场，在未先调查案情的情况下逮捕了五名工人。其他工人因恐惧而不敢发一言。
次日，6月4日，一名名叫张阿妹的女工被捕。

Afterwards we learned that the arrested persons
were handed over to the Jessfield Police Station by the
Settlement Police, and finally were sent to your
Headquarters (? Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commander's
Headquarters) where they are still detained.

Rumours are current that the management is not
content with the number already arrested and intends
to have arrested the workers who took part in the previous
strike, numbering at least 120.

We workers are only interested in our work and have
never acted lawlessly. The management is not justified
in oppressing us to such an extent. To avoid further
development of the dispute and to show pity for the
families of the arrested workers, we request you to
uphold justice and release the workers, who are innocent,
that
at once. We also request you will kindly instruct the
management to fulfil the agreement and to refrain from
arresting workers indiscriminately.

此后我们获悉，被捕人员由租界警察移交给极司菲尔路警察局，最后被送往贵总部（？吴淞-上海警备司令部总部），目前仍被拘押在那里。

有谣言称，资方对已逮捕的人数并不满意，打算逮捕参加上次罢工的工人，人数至少为120人。

我们工人只关心自己的工作，从未有过违法行为。资方如此压迫我们是毫无道理的。为避免纠纷进一步升级，并出于对被捕工人家庭的怜悯，我们请求阁下主持公道，立即释放这些无辜的工人。我们也恳请阁下指示资方履行协议，并停止随意逮捕工人。

The Shanghai Municipality Cotton Weavers' Union,
originally known as the Kung Yik Cotton Mill Employees' Club
of the Chung Nyi Association, was removed on June 1, 1937 from
No.7 King Sung Lee, Brenan Road to No.4, Lane 905 Sung Tuh Fong
off Jessfield Road, O.O.L.

This Union, though it is still in the course of forma-
tion, claims to have 3,500 members which consist of the workers
of the Kung Yik Cotton Mill (British), 150 Robison Road and those
of the China A.B.C. Underwear and Weaving Mill (Chinese) 1099
Connaught Road, O.O.L. Members who join the Union will be
required to pay $1 as the fee for a badge, and they will also
be required to pay a 10 cents monthly membership fee.

Mr. Pan Yen-mung, a private assistant to Mr. Wu Vung

Subject Kung Yik Cotton Mill (British) - Labour Situation.

Made by D.S. Larby    Forwarded by J. Boyne I.S.I.

In connection with the continual unrest existing
among the operatives employed at the Kung Yik Cotton Mill,
150 Robison Road, O.O.L., it has now become increasingly
evident that Mr. Woo Vung-paung (吳文邦) of the local
Tangpu and his assistant Mr. Pan Yeu-nung (潘有農) have
been conducting an active campaign amongst the mill
employees in order to induce them to become members of the
Shanghai 3rd District Cotton Weaving Workers' Union, formerly
known as the Kung Yik Cotton Mill Employees' Club of the
Chung Nyi Association, whose premises have now been removed
from No.7 Ming Sung Li, Brenan Road, to No.4, Lane 905, Zung
Tuh Fang, Jessfield Road.

As a result of the activities of Mr. Woo Vung-paung
and his satellite Mr. Pan Yeu-nung, the Presiding Judge of
the Shanghai Woosung Military Court, namely, Colonel Loh
Ching-dz, has now begun to interest himself in the dispute.
Acting on the instructions of the last named and of Mr.
O.K. Yui, Acting Mayor of Greater Shanghai, Mr. Tsang Taoo-
jang (張楚強), a member of the Bureau of Social Affairs,
and Mr. Yu Yao-chiu (余耀球), committee member of the
local Tangpu visited the factory on the afternoon of June 2
with a view to bringing an end to the present situation.

Acts of intimidation, both within and without the
mill having increased to an alarming extent, the two
representatives named above, decided that it was time that
the Chinese Authorities should take action to curb the
activities of certain of the ringleaders in the present
agitation. With this object in view, Inspectors Tsang Ta-
shan and Chiang Ngoh-wu of the City Government Police Bureau

鉴于罗宾森路150号（外侨居留地以外区域）公益纱厂工人中持续存在的不安情绪，现在越来越明显的是，当地党部的吴文邦（Woo Vung-paung）先生及其助手潘有农（Pan Yeu-nung）先生一直在工厂员工中积极开展活动，以诱导他们加入上海第三区棉织业工人工会，该工会前身为“众义协会公益纱厂职工俱乐部”，其会所已从百老汇路明松里7号迁至极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）宗德坊（Zung Tuh Fang）905弄4号。

由于吴文邦先生及其追随者潘有农先生的活动，上海吴淞军事法庭审判长罗敬之（Loh Ching-dz，音译）上校现在开始关注这一纠纷。根据上述人员及大上海代理市长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui）先生的指示，社会局成员张楚强（Tsang Taoo-jang）先生和当地党部委员余耀球（Yu Yao-chiu）先生于6月2日下午访问了工厂，旨在结束目前的局势。

It was evident that the last named was extremely
embarrassed at being discovered, affording as it did, proof
of his complicity in the present agitation.

The manager of the hotel was advised, that in
view of the nature of the proposed meeting to be held on the
premises, to request the above named occupants of Room No.6
to leave the hotel, which they accordingly did at 9.30 p.m.
approximately.

To date, the position may be briefly described as
this. Mr. Woo Vung-paung, in his anxiety to obtain the
numerical support of the mill workers, has now completely
lost control over them and as a consequence is being subjected
to the orders of coterie composed of certain of the 60
dismissed workers including the eight already mentioned, who
it is rumoured are receiving the support of the Chung Nyi
Association.

In the mill, discipline among the workers is
conspicuous by its absence and it would appear that unless
the Chinese Authorities are prepared to take strong measures,
another strike will eventuate.

At 6 p.m. on the 29/5/37, the operatives employed
in the Spinning Department of the Kung Yik Cotton Mill, 150
Robison Road, O.O.L. went on strike in order to enforce a
demand for a rice allowance of 3 cents per day. Three
representatives of the workers, namely :
(1) Zung Sing-han (陳興漢)
(2) Pan Keh-sing (潘克鑫)
(3) Wang Ah-nyi (王阿二)
who have already represented the mill employees in connection
with previous disputes with the management, then promised to
convey the workers' demand to Mr. E.J. Davies, Manager of the
Mill, whereupon the strikers resumed operations.
On the 31/5/37, the workers - about 400 - employed
in the Weaving Department struck work at 9 a.m. and demanded
that they also should receive a rice allowance of 3 cents
per day.
The mill management then requested the assistance of
Mr. Woo Vung-pang (吳文邦), a representative of the local
Tangpu, to try and effect a settlement of the dispute. Despite
the persuasive efforts of the above named and his assistant
Mr. Pan Yeu-nung (潘有農), both of whom appear to be
singularly incapable of successfully conducting negotiations
with any body of workers, the strikers refused to resume work.
Later, the management requested the S.M.P. to eject the
malcontents but prior to any action being taken, Mr. Woo
suggested to Mr. Davies that the services of the Bureau of
Police rather than those of the S.M.P. be utilized. Mr. Woo
thereupon endeavoured to obtain the necessary police reinforce-
ments but was unsuccessful. The mill management then

5月31日，织布部的工人——约400人——于上午9时罢工，并要求他们也应获得每天3分钱的米贴。
工厂管理层随后请求当地党部代表吴文邦（Woo Vung-pang）先生协助，试图解决纠纷。尽管上述人员及其助手潘有农（Pan Yeu-nung）先生进行了劝说努力，但两人似乎特别缺乏与任何工人群体成功进行谈判的能力，罢工者拒绝复工。

communicated with Mr. Kya Ung-tsau (曹恩超 ), Chief of the
Jessfield Village Branch Bureau, requesting that sub-Inspector
Koo and his subordinates be authorized to co-operate with
the S.M.P. in forcing the strikers to leave the factory.
This request was refused, the Bureau of Police regarding the
proposed procedure as unnecessary.
At this juncture while the S.M.P. were preparing
to take action, the strikers formulated three demands, namely,
1) Restoration of rice allowance of 3 cents per day.
2) A bonus of one day's wages to be paid on the completion of
every fortnight's work.
3) That on Sundays the workers should cease work at 11 a.m.
instead of 4 p.m. as at present.
These demands were at once presented by the workers'
representatives already named to the management who promised
to give an answer within three days. On being informed of
the management's answer, the strikers resumed work.
During the morning, Mr. Davies, who expressed great
dissatisfaction with the actions of Mr. Woo, communicated with
Mr. R. Gordon of Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd. and suggested
that Mr. O.K. Yui, acting Mayor of Greater Shanghai, be
requested to ask the Bureau of Social Affairs to take the
necessary steps to bring about a conclusion of these continual
bickerings.

这一请求被拒绝，警察局认为拟议的程序是不必要的。
就在此时，当工部局警务处正准备采取行动时，罢工者提出了三项要求，即：
1) 恢复每天3分钱的米贴。
2) 每完成两周工作，支付一天工资作为奖金。
3) 周日工人应在上午11时停工，而不是像目前这样在下午4时停工。
这些要求立即由前述工人代表向管理层提出，管理层承诺在三天内给予答复。在得知管理层的答复后，罢工者恢复了工作。
上午期间，Davies 先生对吴先生的行动表示极大不满，他与怡和洋行有限公司的 R. Gordon 先生联系，并建议请求大上海代理市长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui）先生要求社会局采取必要步骤，以终结这些持续的争吵。

The Commissioner,

SHANGHAI

Dear Sir,

With reference to the recent troubles
at our Kung Yik Cotton Mill, 160, Robison Road,
which necessitated the closing of the Mill from
April 1st until May 14th this year, we wish to
record in writing our very sincere appreciation
of the services rendered by your force, both
Foreign and Chinese.

Those on duty within the Mill compound
must have found their task one of extreme monotony
day after day, but our Manager advises us that
nothing was too much trouble for them, that they
were always eager to render any assistance they
could to our staff and always courteous.

We shall esteem it a favour therefore
if you will be good enough to convey our grateful
thanks to all those members of your force under
Inspector Hall from Gordon Road and those in the
Special Branch who were detailed for duty at Kung
Yik Mill during our recent troubles.

We are, dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,

General Managers

Mediation Agreement drawn up between Capital, as

In view of the strike caused through the changing
of the labour system at the Kung Yik Cotton Mill, the
Bureau of Social Affairs, the Tangpu and the Police
Bureau have effected a settlement - with the exception
of the 5% increase which the company sanction of its
own accord - with the following terms which are agreed
to by both sides :

are in the list handed to the Bureau of Social Affairs
by the Management sever their connection with the
Kung Yik Cotton Mill.
2. Of the above mentioned workers, those entitled to
the benefit of the superannuation fund shall be so
paid. Those workers whose superannuation fund amounts
to less than 3 months' wages and those workers not
entitled to the benefit of the superannuation fund
shall have their superannuation fund made up to the
equivalent of three months' wages or receive three
months' wages as compensation.
3. The Company shall not discharge any worker except
when the latter commits insubordination, larceny or
serious misconduct, in which case, the Company will
not only discharge the worker without payment of
compensation but may also have him punished according
to law. Otherwise, should the Company discharge a
worker or workers when changing its labour system,

Date May 6 1937.

Subject The Chung Nyi Association under the "Whampoa" Clique and the Kung
Yik Mill workers.

Made by .................... and .................... Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

Enquiries have been made at various quarters re
the situation of the Kung Yik strike and the following
information has been obtained as a result.

The Kung Yik Mill workers may be divided into
three parties, viz. a majority under the leadership of Chung
Nyi Association; another portion under the local Tangpu and
Social Bureau, and yet another smaller portion who are
independent of either parties.

In view of the little success attained by the
Chung Nyi Association in its recent agitations against the
management of the Kung Yik Mill, it has lost much confidence
with the workers and it is true that a number of them
originally attached to the Chung Nyi Association have gone
over to the Tangpu but this can not be considered a total
failure of the Chung Nyi Association which, besides backing
up by the Fascist Clique of Nanking, possesses considerable
influence among the police officers who would not cease
their activities if there is the least chance of profiting
themselves.

The decision recently arrived at at a joint
meeting of delegates of official organizations at the
Shanghai City Government presided over by Acting Mayor O.K.
Yui that the Social Bureau would be the only competent
organization to solve and mediate in labour troubles, inflicts
a deadly blow on the activities of the Chung Nyi Association.
It is also reported that General Tsai, the Police Commissioner,
has been personally advised by Mr. O.K. Yui to warn his
subordinates not to interfere with labour disputes already
under mediation by the Social Bureau and Tangpu.

制作人 .................... 和 .................... 转呈人：谭绍良警司。

经向各方查询有关公益罢工的情况，获得如下信息。

公益纱厂工人可分为三派，即：大多数人在忠义协会的领导下；另一部分人在当地党部和社会局的领导下；还有一小部分人不依附于任何一方。

鉴于忠义协会最近在反对公益纱厂管理层的煽动活动中收效甚微，它在工人中已失去很多信任，确实有许多原本依附于忠义协会的工人转投党部，但这不能被视为忠义协会的彻底失败，该协会除了得到南京法西斯派系的支持外，在警察官员中也拥有相当大的影响力，只要有一丝牟利的机会，这些警察官员就不会停止活动。

上海市代理市长俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui）主持的官方组织代表联席会议最近作出决定，社会局将是解决和调解劳资纠纷的唯一主管机构，这对忠义协会的活动造成了致命打击。另有报道称，警察局局长蔡将军已亲自接到俞鸿钧先生的建议，警告其下属不要干涉已由社会局和党部调解的劳资纠纷。

Subject Kung Yik Cotton Mill (British) - labour situation.
Made by D.S. Larby................Forwarded by [Signature]

While the strike of operatives employed at the Kung Yik
Cotton Mill, 150 Road (O.O.L.), continues, nevertheless there
are now certain indications which tend to show that a satis-
factory settlement to all concerned may soon be arranged.

This morning (3-5-37), the undersigned learned from Mr.
J.R.Mothersill that negotiations were carried on with Mr. Wong
Ping, representing the Bureau of Social Affairs. Though no
definite arrangement was arrived at, it was evident that the
demands of the workers as elucidated by Mr. Wong were of a far
less preposterous nature than heretofore.

It has now been learned that the workers are proposing to
form a union which will be entirely free from the influences of
the Chung Nyi Association. This union will be known as the
3rd District Cotton Weaving Workers' Union whose membership will
be composed of those workers employed in mills operating in the
Western District.

A meeting of workers took place at No.7, Ming Sung Li on
the 2-5-37 between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. when one Kang Tao-yih
(彭佐一), an employee of the A.B.C. Weaving & Dyeing Mill, Ltd.
1099 Connaught Road (O.O.L.) was elected chairman, and Tsai
Koh-liang (戴國良), an employee of Kung Yik Cotton Mill, and
five others whose names have not as yet been ascertained, were
made members of the preparatory committee responsible for
the organizing of the union, permission for which has already
been granted by the local Tangpu (vide permit No.840).

If, as is suggested, the new union materializes and remains
free from the support or influence of the Chung Nyi Association,
settlement of the present strike situation would seem to be
imminent.
