虽然罗宾森路150号（老闸捕房辖区）公益纱厂工人的罢工仍在继续，但目前有一些迹象表明，不久可能达成令各方满意的和解。

今天上午（1937年5月3日），下述签署人从 J.R. Mothersill 先生处获悉，已与代表社会局的黄平（Wong Ping）先生进行了谈判。虽然尚未达成明确安排，但显然，经黄先生阐明的工人要求远不如以往那样荒谬。

现已获悉，工人们正提议组建一个完全不受忠义协会影响的工会。该工会将称为“第三区棉织业工人工会”，其成员将由在西区运营的各纱厂雇佣的工人组成。

1937年5月2日下午3时至4时，工人们在明松里7号举行了一次会议，会上选举康佐一（Kang Tao-yih，音译，原文括号内为彭佐一，此处依拼音 Kang 对应康，但括号注明彭，故保留括号说明或依惯例处理，此处按指令保留原文不确定加括号，但中文名已给出，故采用给出的中文名，若拼音与汉字不符，以汉字为准，若汉字不确定则保留拼音。指令说“能确定的用当时通行的中文...不确定的保留原文并加括号注明(音译)”。这里给出了汉字“彭佐一”，但拼音是 Kang Tao-yih。通常 Kang 是康，Peng 是彭。这可能是档案错误。根据指令4“照实译出...不要脑补”，我将保留给出的汉字，并在必要时标注差异，或者直接使用给出的汉字。鉴于指令要求“能确定的用...”，这里汉字已给出，我使用汉字。但为了严谨，若拼音明显冲突，可加注。不过指令主要针对无法确定的情况。此处直接使用给出的中文名。）——康托伊（Kang Tao-yih，音译，原文注：彭佐一），康纳路（Connaught Road）1099号、老闸捕房辖区 ABC 纺织印染厂有限公司的一名雇员当选为主席，公益纱厂雇员戴国良（Tsai Koh-liang，音译，原文注：戴國良）及其他五名姓名尚未查明的人被选为负责组建工会的筹备委员会成员，当地党部已批准组建该工会（参见许可证第840号）。

如果如所建议的那样，新工会得以成立并保持不受忠义协会的支持或影响，目前罢工局势的解决似乎指日可待。

Relative to the strike of operatives at the Kung

Kung Primary School, 121 Brenan Road, O.O.L. after which the

assistance from the Government Authorities.

It is possible, however, that the notice referred
to above is in the nature of a bluff as it has been learned
that at a secret meeting of about a dozen of the leading
agitators in the present strike, held in the premises of the
Chung Nyi Association at approximately 12 mid-night (20/4/37),
it was decided that the strikers should attend en masse
at the North Railway Station in the afternoon of the 21/4/37
for the purpose of obtaining accommodation on the 4 p.m. train
to Nanking where they intended to petition the Government
Authorities for assistance in the settlement of the strike.

This move, however, in view of the present weather conditions
has been indefinitely postponed.

Subject Kung Yik Cotton Mill (British) - Strike Situation.
Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by J. Byrne O S I

In connection with the strike of operatives employed
at the Kung Yik Cotton Mill (British), 150 Robison Road, two
notices pertaining to the dispute were posted outside the
mill on the 18.4.37 at 12.30 p.m.
On one notice it was stated that registration of male
and female workers of whom the mill management approved
would be commenced on the 19.4.37. Following completion of
this registration a further notice informing the workers of
the date of resumption of operations would then be posted.
The other notice which was chopped by Mr. Pan Kung-chan,
Chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs, informed the strikers
that the action of the management in commencing registration
of the workers met with the approval of the Bureau. In
addition to the above, the notice stated that a proper
settlement of the present outstanding differences between the
management and its employees would receive the wholehearted
attention of the Bureau.
Following the posting of these two notices, in the after-
noon of the 18.4.37, about 100 strikers gathered in the
premises of the Chung Nyi Association, No. 7 Ming Sung Li,
Brenan Road, O.O.L., and held a meeting at which one Tai Koh
Liang(戴國良) presided. The aforementioned person addressed
the meeting and stated that the workers' union had received
a letter (No. 7929) from the Bureau of Social Affairs.
Contained in this letter were instructions to the effect that
the union was to appoint two representatives to attend a
meeting of the interested parties, with a view to obtaining
a settlement satisfactory to all concerned. This meeting was
scheduled to take place at the Bureau on the 20.4.37.

关于受雇于老靶子路罗宾森路150号公益纱厂（英商）的工人罢工一事，有两份与纠纷有关的通知于1937年4月18日中午12点30分张贴在纱厂外。
其中一份通知称，经纱厂管理层批准的男女工人的登记工作将于1937年4月19日开始。登记完成后，将再张贴一份通知，告知工人复工日期。
另一份通知盖有社会局局长潘公展先生的印章，通知罢工工人，管理层开始登记工人的举动已得到社会局的批准。此外，该通知还指出，社会局将全心全意关注目前管理层与其雇员之间尚未解决的差异，并寻求妥善解决。
在这两份通知张贴后，即1937年4月18日下午，约100名罢工工人聚集在老靶子路明松里7号众谊协会场所内，并举行了一次会议，由戴国良主持。前述人物在会上发言，称工会已收到社会局的一封信（第7929号）。信中指示工会指派两名代表参加有关各方的会议，以期达成令各方满意的解决方案。该会议定于1937年4月20日在社会局举行。

released, no action being taken by the Chinese Authorities
despite assurances given by Mr. O. K. Yui, Acting Mayor of
Greater Shanghai, that full protection would be given to all
employees desirous of returning to work. Considerable
rowdyism occurred in the vicinity of the mill after the
release of the picket by the Chinese Authorities, but the
workers eventually left the locality without in fact clashing
with the police of either jurisdiction. It was noticeable
that the Bureau of Police took little or no action to control
or disperse the crowds which gathered, this duty being
performed by the Municipal Police.

Later, it was learned that representatives of the
strikers had expressed the intention of visiting the Special
Branch, Shanghai Municipal Police Headquarters, on the morning
of the 20.4.37 with a view to requesting mediation by the
Municipal Police. Realising, however, that this was likely
to prejudice any chances of obtaining assistance from the
Bureau of Social Affairs at the meeting arranged for the
afternoon of the 20.4.37, the proposed visit was postponed for
the time being.

The situation to date is therefore a stalemate with no
immediate prospect of a settlement being reached. Judging by
the trend of reports and the information to hand, there would
appear to be little or no doubt that the majority of the
operatives would be only too glad to return to work, their
present actions and demeanour being nothing more than the
result of the incessant threats of intimidation propagated by
Tai Koh-liang and his followers.

获释，尽管大上海代理市长俞鸿钧先生曾保证将给予所有希望复工的雇员充分保护，但中国当局并未采取任何行动。在中国当局释放纠察队员后，纱厂附近发生了相当严重的骚乱，但工人们最终离开了该地区，实际上并未与任何管辖区域的警察发生冲突。值得注意的是，警察局（Bureau of Police）对聚集的人群几乎没有采取任何控制或驱散行动，这一职责由工部局警务处承担。

后来获悉，罢工者代表曾打算于1937年4月20日上午访问上海公共租界工部局警务处总部特务科，旨在请求工部局警务处进行调解。然而，他们意识到此举可能会损害在定于1937年4月20日下午举行的会议上从社会局获得援助的机会，因此暂时推迟了拟议的访问。

因此，截至目前的局势处于僵持状态，短期内没有达成解决方案的前景。根据报告的趋势和现有信息判断，毫无疑问，大多数工人非常乐意返回工作岗位，他们目前的行动和表现不过是戴国良及其追随者不断散布的恐吓威胁所致。

proceeded to the locality and noted that by 10 a.m.,
approximately 1,000 strikers had assembled. Numbers of
pickets waving flags inscribed with the characters
"Picket of Kung Yik Cotton Mill," were parading up and
down Brenan Road in the vicinity of the meeting.
At about 10.45 a.m. the workers formed a procession
and walked along Brenan Road for about 100 yards prior to
their entering Chapei in order to proceed along Chungsan 中山
Road to the Civic Centre where they (the workers) intended
to visit the Bureau of Social Affairs and request for
assistance in the settlement of the strike.
In addition to the flags displayed by the pickets,
one large banner was also carried by the body of the workers.
On the banner, a number of Chinese characters were inscribed,
which could be freely translated as "An appeal by the workers
of the Kung Yik Cotton Mill for assistance from the Kuomintang
and the City Government in order that work may be resumed."
Subsequently, the procession was dispersed by the
Chapei Police whereupon the strikers returned to the
premises of the Chung Yri Association, No.7 Ming Sung Li,
Brenan Road, afterwards proceeding to their respective homes.

Date April 15, 1937.

Subject Kung Yik Cotton Mill (British) - Strike Situation

Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by I bayau D.S.I

Attached herewith is a copy of a letter addressed
to Jardine Matheson & Co. Ltd, which purports to specify
the grievances of the striking operatives of the Kung Yik
Cotton Mill.

This morning, April 15, D.S.I. Shih and the undersigned
were given to understand by Mr. J.R. Mothersill, that
Mr. O.K. Yui, acting on behalf of the Shanghai City Government
had assured Jardine Matheson & Co. Ltd that the Bureau of
Police would take all necessary precautions to prevent any
intimidation of employees who wished to resume work. On the
strength of this promise, the Kung Yik Mill Management
within the next few days propose to post a notice at the
entrance to the factory, inviting the workers to resume
work, the Management reserving the right to select those
whom it regards as satisfactory. It is the intention of
the management to have this notice chopped by the Bureau
of Social Affairs, thereby, it is hoped, encouraging the
operatives to resume their duties.
（印：POLICE STATION NO 13 CHAPEL ROAD 16 APR.）

This morning, April 15, thirty-eight members of the
maintenance department resumed work, subsequent to which it
was rumoured that members of the Chung Hyi Association were
endeavouring to influence the strikers to intimidate these
loyal employees, thereby forcing them to cease work.

Mr. H.J. Davies, Manager of the Mill, Mr. J.R.Mothersill
Mr. R. Gordon, in addition to the Officer in charge Gordon
Road Station, are fully cognizant of the situation to date.

Shanghai, April, 14th, 1937.

The Manager,
Jardine, Matheson & Co.,Ltd.,
27 The Bund, SHANGHAI

Dear Sir,

We the undersigned take the liberty to write you these few lines not only in the interest of the livings of more than 3,000 workers but for the benefit of the Hung Yik Cotton Mill and the Sino-British relations as well.

We are the workers of the Hung Yik Cotton Mill, which is understood to be under the management of your esteemed firm. Until recently, we had been in perfect harmony with the authorities of the Mill, which may be verified by the satisfactory result of the operations of the Mill during the past years. Since the appointment last year of Ching Tuck-fang as engineer of the Mill, our treatment has been considerably worsened, such as the manhandling of the workers, disengagement of the old hands, etc., etc. These resulted in the general strike on February 19, 1937, which was called off through the mediation of the Chinese Party and Government authorities, who asked the workers to resume operations prior to formal negotiations: during the period of more than one month following the resumption of work, not only the demands of the workers were not accepted by the Mill authorities, but also Ching Tuck-fang, instead of modifying his attitude, intensified his maltreatment of the operatives. On April 1, 1937, he struck Chang Ho-sheng of the Fine Cotton Yarn Dept. without reason so seriously that the latter bled in his mouth on the spot. This again caused a "go-slow" strike. Immediately afterwards, Ching Tuck-fang called for more than 100 police, who, under the former's direction, manhandled all the workers of the Mill without discrimination with the result that 19 hands were seriously injured and over 70 received skin wounds. All these are actually responsible for the present standstill of the operations of the Mill, which is naturally much affected financially although the workers are forced to be put in a desperate state.

Although workers, we do realize the pleasant relations between Great Britain and China. We are really compelled to resort to strike, which, however, does not mean any ill feeling against Great Britain and your esteemed firm, but is a reaction of Ching Tuck-fang's high-handed attitude toward the employees.

上海，1937年4月14日。

经理先生，
怡和洋行有限公司，
上海外滩27号

尊敬的先生：

我们署名者冒昧致函，不仅是为了三千多名工人的生计着想，也是为了鸿益纱厂以及中英关系的利益。

我们是鸿益纱厂的工人，据悉该厂由贵行管理。直到最近，我们与厂方当局一直保持着完美的和谐关系，过去几年工厂运营的满意结果可以证实这一点。自从去年任命程德芳（Ching Tuck-fang，音译）为工厂工程师以来，我们的待遇大大恶化，例如殴打工人、解雇老员工等等。这导致了1937年2月19日的大罢工，此次罢工在中国党及政府当局的调解下被取消，当局要求工人在正式谈判前复工：在复工后的一个多月期间，厂方当局不仅没有接受工人的要求，而且程德芳非但没有改变态度，反而加剧了对操作工的虐待。1937年4月1日，他无故严重殴打了细纱部的张和生（Chang Ho-sheng，音译），致使后者当场口吐鲜血。这再次引发了“怠工”罢工。紧接着，程德芳召来了100多名警察，在他的指挥下，不分青红皂白地殴打了全厂所有工人，导致19名工人重伤，70多人受皮外伤。所有这些实际上造成了目前工厂运营的停滞，虽然工人们被迫陷入绝望境地，但工厂在财务上自然受到了很大影响。

虽然是工人，但我们确实意识到英国与中国之间的良好关系。我们实在是被迫采取罢工行动，但这并不意味着对英国和贵行有任何恶意，而是对程德芳对待雇员的高压态度的反应。

Made by D.S. Larby Forwarded by J Boyne D.S.I.

In connection with the strike of operatives at the Kung
Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, it is reported that at 2 p.m.
on the 11/4/37, a meeting of about 50 workers was held in the
Kung Yih Cotton Mill Employees Club situated at No.7 Ming Sung
Lee, Brenan Road, when it was decided that the following demands
should be put to the management:-
1. That in the event of the management deciding to close down
the mill, compensation equivalent to 18 months' wages be
given to each worker.
2. That any medical expenses incurred by the workers who were
injured in the recent fracas be paid by the mill management.
3. That a retiring gratuity equivalent to one month's wages for
every year of service be paid to those employees who retire
after 10 or more years' service.
4. That the instigator of the present dispute, one King Teh
Fong, labour manager of the mill, be severely punished.

Summarized translation of a petition submitted to the
Nantao District Court by Lawyer Ao Sen on behalf of
Mr Zing Teh-fong and his three assistants in connection
with the case of assault brought against them by certain
workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill.

APPLICATION FOR REMAND AND EXPLANATION OF FACTS.

Following the abolition of the contracting system and
the adoption of direct control by the management, the workers
of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill went on strike on February 19,
1937, but, through the mediation of the Bureau of Social
Affairs, they resumed work on February 27.

On March 31. 1937 Mr Waung Tsoh Sung (汪作松), attached
to the Bureau of Social Affairs interviewed the manager of
the mill and stated that the workers had submitted eight
demands. At 5.30 p.m. the same evening information was
received that the workers would create trouble in the mill.
Mr Davies, Manager of the Mill informed Gordon Road Police
Station and requested assistance. At 5.30 a.m. April 1,
Mr Davies visited the working rooms and found that the night
shift workers had put on their day clothes and that the day
shift workers had not put on their working clothes. After
questioning, the workers adopted a defiant attitude and threw
spindles at Mr. Davies. At the same time it was learned that
Mr Hargreaves, Chief of the Cloth Department, had been
assaulted and injured. Although one foreign and four Chinese
policeman were on duty outside the mill gates they were not
in a position to enter owing to the question of jurisdiction.
Subsequently with the consent of the Officer in charge of the
Robison Road Sub-Police Bureau, the Shanghai Municipal Police
were permitted to enter the factory. Mr Davies then telephoned
to Gordon Road Police Station requesting for reinforcements.
He, then accompanied by another foreigner, went to the rescue
of Mr Hargreaves. When he returned, twenty Indian Policemen

敖森律师代表徐德芳先生及其三名助手，就公义纱厂部分工人对其提起的殴打案，向南市地方法院提交的诉状摘要译文。

申请还押候审及事实说明。

随着包工制的废除和管理层直接控制模式的采用，公义纱厂工人于1937年2月19日罢工，但在社会局的调解下，他们于2月27日复工。

1937年3月31日，隶属于社会局的汪作松先生（Waung Tsoh Sung）会见了该厂经理，并表示工人已提出八项要求。同日傍晚5时30分，接获情报称工人将在厂内滋事。厂长达维斯（Davies）先生通知戈登路巡捕房并请求协助。4月1日凌晨5时30分，达维斯先生视察车间，发现夜班工人已换上便服，而白班工人尚未穿上工作服。经询问，工人态度强硬并向达维斯先生投掷纱锭。与此同时，获悉布匹部主任哈格里夫斯（Hargreaves）先生遭到殴打受伤。虽然有一名外籍巡捕和四名华捕在厂门外执勤，但因管辖权问题无法进入。随后，经罗宾森路分巡捕房主管警官同意，上海公共租界工部局警务处获准进入工厂。达维斯先生随即致电戈登路巡捕房请求增援。随后，他在另一名外籍人士的陪同下，前去营救哈格里夫斯先生。当他返回时，二十名印度巡捕

in charge of a British Subject named Hall, had arrived.
The workers, at this time, were throwing iron bars, weighing
about two pounds each, out of the windows. Owing to lack
of police strength, Mr Hall telephoned for the Reserve Unit,
the vans arrived approximately one hour later. During this
period the workers were given the opportunity of leaving the
premises. The female workers tried to leave but were prevent-
ed from doing so by the male workers. When the Reserve Unit
arrived a tense situation prevailed. The above are the
facts related in brief.

It should be noted that the workers committed acts of
violence. The ██████ General Manager requested for police
assistance in order to cope with the situation. There must
be some ulterior motive as the workers have maliciously
accused the defendants. The workers, who, number more than
2,500, were armed with iron bars etc, while the defendants
were unarmed and thus were not in a position to injure the
workers.

In view of the fact that workers might seize the
opportunity to attack them during the meeting, the defendants
request your honourable Court to question the plaintiffs
first and then remand the case for a further hearing in order
that the defendants may be questioned and so avoid unfortunate
incidents.

At 11 a.m. April 5, 1937, a notice was posted in the
Kung Yih Cotton Mill Employees' Club of the Chung Nyi Associat-
ion, No. 7 Ming Sung Lee, Brenan Road, to the effect that in
addition to the demands already presented to the management,
the following three demands would be added to the list:-
(1) That Zing Teh-fong(徐德芳), the Labour Manager, be
punished.
(2) That compensation and medical expenses be issued to
the injured workers.
(3) That wages be issued during the period of the strike .

All No. 1 and No. 2 foremen of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill
have contributed $1 each to the Employees' Club of the Chung
Nyi Association. The money thus subscribed will be utilised
for the payment of travelling expenses for the representatives
of the workers, whilst proceeding to interview the various
authorities.

Strikers' pickets were active yesterday, April 5, 1937. At
2.30 p.m. pickets detained at the corner of Penang and Robison
Roads one Zung Hsing-kung, a coolie employed by the Kung Yih
Cotton Mill. They attempted to escort him to the Employees'
Club, 7 Ming Sung Li, Brenan Road. The pickets were prevented
from carrying out their intention by the arrival of the Chapei
Police, who brought both parties to the Robison Road Sub-
Station. After enquiries Zung was escorted back to the mill
premises by the Chapei Police.

prevent the departure of trucks loaded with cotton goods from

During the afternoon of April 2, 1937, seven representatives
of the workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill called on officials
of the local Kuomintang, Feng Ling Jao, off Route Ghisi,
the Chinese Ratepayers' Association, 59 Hongkong Road, and

Nord in order to present a petition and to request for
assistance in the present dispute. It will be recalled
that a similar visit was paid to officials of the Shanghai
City Government and the Bureau of Social Affairs during
the morning of April 2, 1937.

With reference to the activities of the workers, information
has been received that the strikers have formed six picket
groups, each consisting of thirty men for the purpose of
preventing workers from breaking the strike.

At 6 p.m. April 2, 1937 a staff foreman of the mill
named Wong Tong Zung (王棟成) was molested by a number of
strikers whilst he was riding in a ricksha near Brenan Piece.
The foreman appealed to the Chapel Police for assistance.
He was escorted to the 6th Division Station for safety and
later permitted to leave.

During the morning of April 3, 1937 information was
received from the mill management that the strikers intended
to assault the mill on Monday morning, but confirmation to
that effect is lacking. Rumours are, however, current that
the strikers intend to assault Mr. Zang Teh-fong (臧德芳),
Labour Manager of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill.

Social Affairs named Wong Tsah-sung (王乍生) visited the

Translation of a petition presented to the City
Government on April 2 by workers of the Kung Yih
Cotton Mill.
----------
On March 22 the petitioners submitted appeals to the
local Tangpu and the Bureau of Social Affairs in which they
complained of the bad treatment accorded workers by the management
and of assaults on workers by new staff employees, and requested
mediation in the dispute.
At 6 p.m. April 1, Zing Teh-fong(秦德芳), a new staff
employee, assaulted and injured Tsang Ho-sung(张和尚), a worker
in the Fine Yarn Department of the Mill. The petitioners were
annoyed at Zing's brutality and demanded the reasons for the
assault. The management immediately convened a meeting which
was attended by all foremen. While the foremen were relating
the circumstances regarding the incident, about one hundred
Chinese and foreign policemen arrived. Zing Teh-fong instructed
the police officers to assault the workers, as a result many
of our number were injured.
During the assault, the mill gates were closed, thus
preventing the escape of the workers. Members of the Bureau
of Police were not permitted to enter the mill by the management
and the Shanghai Municipal Police. Eventually the management
allowed the gates to be opened and the workers were permitted
to leave the mill premises.
The action of the members of the Shanghai Municipal
Police in preventing the Bureau of Police officers from entering
the factory is an insult to the dignity of the country. The
petitioners hereby request that a responsible officer be
appointed to take up the matter with the Shanghai Municipal
Council.

Mr. O.K. Yui,
Acting Mayor of Greater Shanghai.

公义纱厂工人于4月2日向市政府提交的请愿书译文。
----------
3月22日，具状人向当地塘浦（Tangpu，音译）机构和社会局提交申诉，投诉管理层虐待工人以及新聘员工殴打工人，并请求调解纠纷。
4月1日下午6时，新聘员工秦德芳（Zing Teh-fong）殴打并致伤该厂细纱部工人张和尚（Tsang Ho-sung）。具状人对秦的暴行感到愤怒，并要求说明殴打原因。管理层立即召开会议，所有领班均出席。正当领班们叙述事件经过时，约一百名中外巡捕到达。秦德芳指令巡捕殴打工人，导致我方多人受伤。
在殴打期间，工厂大门紧闭，阻止工人逃离。警察局成员未被允许进入工厂，这是由管理层和上海公共租界工部局警务处所为。最终，管理层允许打开大门，工人获准离开工厂区域。
上海公共租界工部局警务处成员阻止警察局官员进入工厂的行为，是对国家尊严的侮辱。具状人特此请求指派一名负责官员就此事项与上海公共租界工部局进行交涉。

致：
大上海代市长 俞鸿钧（O.K. Yui）先生。

REPORT
Date April 5, 1937
Subject Meeting of workers of Kung Yih Cotton Mill.
Made by D.S.I. Umemoto. Forwarded by D.I. Nakamura
Information has been obtained from certain Japanese sources to the effect that at 7.20 a.m. April 2, 1937, workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill held a conference at No. 7 Min Sung Li (民生里), Brenan Road. Boo Vung Ming (蒲凤鸣), Yang Chun Ying (杨占英) and Lee Ts Bing (李子平) of the Chung Nyi Association attended the meeting, which was presided over by Boo Vung Ming.
In the course of the meeting, Boo Vung Ming reported that a member of the local Tangpu came to the office of the Chung Nyi Association on April 1 to make enquiries into the strike also and proposed that a delegate be sent to the Bureau of Social Affairs at 9.30 a.m. April 3.
It is learned that the following resolutions were passed:-
1) That the workers of the Ewo Cotton Mill, Yangtsepoo Road, be induced to go on a sympathetic strike. For this purpose delegates have already been sent to the Eastern District to keep in touch with workers of the Ewo Cotton Mill.
2) That two groups, each consisting of seven persons, be organized to visit the hospital and to express their sympathy with the wounded workers.
3) That the running-dogs of the management of the mill in question be checked in their activities.
4) That picketing and communication Corps be organised.
5) That the punishment of those responsible for the assault on the workers be demanded.
6) That a manifesto be issued requesting the Chinese Authorities to deal with the matter impartially.
Asst. Commissioner (J).
D. S. I.

从某些日本方面获得情报称，1937年4月2日上午7时20分，公益纱厂工人在白伦路（Brenan Road）民生里7号举行会议。忠义协会（Chung Nyi Association）的蒲凤鸣（Boo Vung Ming）、杨占英（Yang Chun Ying）和李子平（Lee Ts Bing）出席了会议，会议由蒲凤鸣主持。
在会议过程中，蒲凤鸣报告说，当地党部的一名成员于4月1日来到忠义协会办公室，也就罢工一事进行查询，并建议于4月3日上午9时30分派代表前往社会局。
据悉，会议通过了以下决议：-
1) 劝诱杨树浦路怡和纱厂（Ewo Cotton Mill）的工人举行同情罢工。为此，已派遣代表前往东区，与怡和纱厂工人保持联系。
2) 组织两个小组，每组七人，前往医院慰问受伤工人，表达同情。
3) 遏制该厂管理层走狗的活动。
4) 组织纠察队和通讯队。
5) 要求惩办殴打工人的责任人。
6) 发表宣言，请求中国当局公正处理此事。

Subject Kung Yih Cotton Mill (British) - strike situation.

Made by D.S. Lockwood Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I.

Between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m. April 1, 1937, a meeting of
about 150 workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill was held in the
premises of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill Employees' Club of the Chung
Nyi Association, No.7 Ming Sung Li, Brenan Road. One Tsau Hung
Chi (周宏基), a prominent member of the Association took an
active part in the discussion.

During the meeting the following seven workers of the
Kung Yih Cotton Mill were selected from among the workers, to
proceed to the City Government during the forenoon of April 2
to submit an appeal for mediation in connection with their demands
for better treatment:-
Liao Chung Nyi (廖仲義); Tai Koh Liang (戴國良);
Tsang Woo Zan (張武山); Wei Pao Pao (魏宝宝);
Tsu Foo Ying (朱富英); Lee Ching Lung (李金隆);
Loh Nien Dee (陸年弟).

At 9.30 a.m. April 2, the representatives together with
19 other workers, who, it is alleged, were injured during the clash
between the Police and strikers on April 1, met in the premises of
the Chung Nyi Association, No.7 Ming Sung Li, Brenan Road, and
made final preparations for the visit to the City Government
authorities. At 10.30 a.m. April 2, the representatives left in
a removing van to call on officials of the City Government and
Bureau of Social Affairs in order to present a petition and to
request for assistance in the present dispute. They will pay a
similar call on officials of the local Tangpu Headquarters, Feng
Ling Jao, at 2.30 p.m. of April 2, 1937.

D.S. Lockwood.

Subject Kung Yih Cotton Mill (British), 150 Robison Road - strike declared

Made by D.S. Lockwood Forwarded by Thoyne D.S.I

At 5.45 a.m. April 1, 1937, approximately 3,000 day and night shift workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill declared a strike and commenced to destroy machinery and equipment in order to force the management to accept a series of demands which had been drawn up by Lee Ching Loong and six representatives of workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill and presented to the local Tangpu Headquarters for approval on March 22, 1937, (vide S.B. report March 23, 1937). Owing to the refusal of the workers to leave the premises the management requested the assistance of the Municipal Police. Following the arrival of the Police an affray took place during which a number of workers were injured. The Police succeeded in ejecting the workers from the mill premises. No arrests were affected.

（印：RECEIVED 2 APR. 1937 SHANGHAI）

At about 2.30 p.m. March 31, 1937 one named Wong Tsoh-sung (汪竹聲), a member of the Bureau of Social Affairs called on Mr. Zing Tuh Fong, labour contractor of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill and informed him that a series of demands had been presented to the Bureau by representatives of the workers and suggested that a meeting be arranged between the management and the workers' representatives. No definite reply regarding this suggestion was given by the management to Mr. Wong, who, subsequently left the mill. After leaving the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, Mr. Wong proceeded to the Kung Yih Cotton Mill Employees' Club of the Chung Nyi Association, No.7 Ming Seng Li, Brenan Road, O.O.L. and informed the workers of the result of the interview with the management.

At 8 p.m. the same day, the management informed Gordon Road Station to the effect that trouble was likely to break out during the night March 31 - April 1. Precautionary

1937年4月1日上午5时45分，公益纱厂约3000名日班和夜班工人宣布罢工，并开始破坏机器和设备，以迫使管理层接受由李全龍（Lee Ching Loong）和六名公益纱厂工人代表拟定、并于1937年3月22日提交当地党部总部批准的一系列要求（参见1937年3月23日特别支部报告）。由于工人拒绝离开工厂，管理层请求工部局警务处协助。警察到达后发生了斗殴，多名工人受伤。警察成功将工人驱逐出厂区。未实施逮捕。

1937年3月31日下午2时30分左右，社会局一名名为汪竹聲（Wong Tsoh-sung）的成员拜访了公益纱厂劳工包工头郑土芳（Zing Tuh Fong）先生，告知他工人代表已向该局提出一系列要求，并建议安排管理层与工人代表举行会议。管理层未对王先生的建议给予明确答复，王先生随后离开工厂。离开公益纱厂后，王先生前往白伦路民生里7号（原文如此，前文为Ming Sung Li，此处为Ming Seng Li，均指民生里）忠义协会公益纱厂职工俱乐部，向工人们通报了与管理层会谈的结果。

At about 10 a.m. on March 22, Lee Ching Loong

deduction in pay effected last year be abolished;

strike;

workers be signed if the above demands are accepted by the
management;

The workers' representatives were received by Lee
Wei Hsiun (李維勳), a committee member of the Tangpu, who
advised them to wait for a reply.

the local Tangpu at the instigation of Tsau Hung Kyi (周洪基),

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by J. Boyne. D.S.I.
At a meeting held at No.7 Ming Seng Li, Brenan Road,
between 6.30 p.m. and 7.30 p.m. on March 11, Tsau Hong-kyi, a
responsible member of the Chung Nyi Association addressed some
30 workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, and
stated that Mayor Wu had now refused to negotiate with the Mill
Management regarding the demands put forward on March 7. There-
fore their plan would have to be abandoned. Tsau then said
that according to Mr. Yao Kwang-nsi, the workers of the Kung Yih
Cotton Mill should organize an independant labour union them-
selves, whilst the Chung Nyi Association would surreptitiously
render assistance. By so doing, the Chung Nyi Association would
be free from the accusation that it is dominating the workers'
movement. At the termination of the meeting, Tsau Hong-kyi
urged the workers to follow his advise, stating that in case
the mill management discharge any more workers, their union,
if organized in time, will prove to be a useful weapon to cope
with the situation.
Shih

About 50 workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison
Road, held a meeting at 7, Ming Seng Li, Brenan Road, between
9 p.m. and 10 p.m. on March 7, when the following resolutions
were discussed and passed:-
1. That the Mill Management be requested to pay the workers
full wages for the period of the recent strike;
2. That the Mill Management be requested to recognize the
Kung Yih Cotton Mill Employees' Club, and issue a
monthly allowance of $60 to the Club;
3. That the Management be requested to deduct membership
fees from the workers' wages each month for the Club.
(Amount of membership fee to be fixed later).
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH / 10 MAR 1937 / SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）
4. That the Management be requested not to engage any
new employees;
5. That the Management be requested not to discharge any more
of the present workers.
The meeting was presided over by Tseu Hong-kyi, a member
of the Chung Nyi Association.
At 9 p.m. on March 9, Tseu Hong-kyi assembled some twenty
workers of the Kung Yih Mill to his office at No.7 Ming Seng Li,
Brenan Road, and told them that the above resolutions had been
forwarded to Mayor Wu through Mr. Yao Kwang-nai and the Mayor
would soon open negotiations with the Mill Management for a
solution. Tseu claimed that the present movement had won the
sympathy of the workers of the □□ Cotton Mills in Yangtsepoo
District.

Between 9 p.m. and 11 p.m. on March 4, about 20
workers of the Spinning Department of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill,
150 Robison Road, held a meeting at No.7 Ming Seng Lee, Brenan
Road, O.O.L., the office of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill Employees'
Club of the Chung Nyi Association, and discussed the results of
the recent strike. Lee Tien Tsoo, a member of the Chung Nyi
Association who presided over the meeting, stated that the only
persons to benefit as a result of the strike were Tsang Tsao Jang,
a representative of the Bureau of Social Affairs, Wong Tsoh Ping,
Committee Member of the 3rd District Spinning Union and a few
discharged workers, while the strikers had had to sustain a loss
of nine days' pay without benefit. Lee Tien Tsoo also informed
the meeting that he had learned that the mill had decided to
discharge a further batch of No.2 foremen on March 28. In
conclusion he urged that measures be adopted to cope with the
situation. The following resolutions were discussed and passed:-

1. That a meeting of the foremen of all departments of
the mill be held in the mill's dining hall during the tiffin
hours on March 5th to discuss the declaration of another strike
for the purpose of submitting further demands.

2. That another meeting be held in the Club office at
No.7 Ming Seng Lee, Brenan Road at 8.30 p.m. on March 5th to
discuss the situation further.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / NEWS. No. D... / Date ... 37）

Subject The Kang Yih Cotton Mill (British) - strike situation.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by J. Bayne D.S.I

As a result of the change of attitude of the Chung Hyi
Association and the consequent absence of the pickets at all
approaches to the mill, about 600 strikers (approximately 60%
of the total night shift complement) resumed work at 5.30 p.m.
on February 26th without the occurrence of any untoward incident.
About 860 hands (approx. 80% of the day shift workers) turned
up for work this morning, February 27th. The situation is now
practically normal.

When the notice, posted at the Mill Gate by the Chung
Hyi Association, was removed by the mill management in the
afternoon of the February 26th, another notice, similarly
worded, was re-posted at the mill gate late on the night of
February 27th by a member of the Chung Hyi Association.

Since the resumption of work by the strikers, no responsi-
ble members of the Chung Hyi Association have attended office
at 7 Ming Seng Li, Brenan. The activities of members of the
Association are being closely watched.

Shih

Mr. Chang Yin Chun (張蔭春), officer in charge
Investigation Department of the local Tangpu, telephoned this

Translation of Proclamation No. 4416 issued on
February 24, 1937, by the Shanghai Kuomintang
Headquarters and the Bureau of Social Affairs.
----------
The action taken by the Kung Yih Cotton Mill,
a British owned concern, in abolishing the contract
system is beneficial to the workers, and there should
be no dispute since both parties have consulted together
and decided upon certain measures for settlement.
The workers, however, went on strike, being instigated
by the bad elements, and submitted demands on this pretext.
They disregard the peace and order of the locality.
Although after repeated advices given by delegates of
the Tangpu and Bureau, a large number of the workers
have awakened to their senses, yet a number of the
bad characters among the workers have compelled their
followers to prevent workers from resuming work. Such
activities are unlawful. Investigations will be made
regarding the ringleaders and if found, they will be
severely punished. This proclamation is jointly issued
by the Tangpu and Bureau warning all workers of the mill
to resume work forthwith and not to wait any longer.

Standing Committee of the Tangpu :
Tao Pah Chuen
Pan Kung Chai
Tung Ying Bah

Commissioner of the Social Bureau :
Pan Kung Chai.

1937年2月24日由上海国民党市党部和社会局发布的第4416号告示译文。
----------
英商公怡棉纺厂废除包身制之举对工人有利，既然双方已共同协商并决定了某些解决措施，本不应发生争议。
然而，工人受不良分子煽动，借此借口提出要求进行罢工。他们无视地方的和平与秩序。
虽然经过党部和社会局代表的反复劝告，大量工人已醒悟，但工人中的一批坏分子仍强迫其追随者阻止工人复工。此类活动属非法行为。将对首恶分子进行调查，一经查获，将严惩不贷。此告示由党部和社会局联合发布，警告全厂工人立即复工，不得再行等待。

Chow Hung-chi (周宏基), member of the Chung
Nyi Association, addressed some 100 foremen and strikers
of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, in the office of the Strikers'

Subject The Kung Yih Cotton Mill - strike situation.
Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by J. Boyce D.S.I.

The Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, remained closed this morning, February 24th, and although a small number of workers turned out for work at 5.30 p.m. on February 23rd and 5.30 a.m. on 24th, they were sent away by the Management; the number being insufficient for resumption of operations.

At about 3 p.m. on February 23rd, a meeting was held at No.7, Ming Seng Li, Brenan Road, the office of the "Kung Yih Cotton Mill Employees Club of the Chung Nyi Association" between members of the Chung Nyi Association and the representatives of the strikers of the Kung Yih Mill. Lee Tien T'soo presided at the meeting, during which it was decided to form a picket outside the mill consisting of thirty persons, with the object of preventing workers from resuming work. The group was immediately organized and Liao Tsoong Kyi (廖榮義) and Yao Yoong Seng (姚永生) were appointed to take charge of the picket. It is learned that during the afternoon of February 23rd, many workers were warned by members of this group that they would be assaulted if they come to work.

At about 5 p.m. on February 23rd, Mr. Yao Kweng-nai, Chief of the West Gate Branch Bureau of the Chinese Police Bureau, visited the office of the Kung Yih Mill Employees' Club and held a meeting at which the following four forewomen, whom the Mill Management had decided to discharge for agitation among the strikers, attended:-
1. Ah Ling (阿林);
2. Yoong Tseng (雲珍);
3. Foong Ying (鳳英);
4. Yoong Kwei (雲桂).
Tseu Heng Kyi and Lee Tsao Zung were also present at the

2月23日下午3时许，在“众毅会公怡棉纺厂职工俱乐部”办公室（白利南路明生里7号）举行了众毅会成员与公怡厂罢工代表之间的会议。李天素（Lee Tien T'soo，音译）主持会议，会上决定在厂外组建一支由三十人组成的纠察队，目的是阻止工人复工。该小组随即成立，廖榮義（Liao Tsoong Kyi）和姚永生（Yao Yoong Seng）被任命负责纠察队。据悉，2月23日下午，许多工人受到该小组成员的警告，如果他们来上班将会遭到袭击。

At 12.15 p.m. February 23, Mr. Yao Kwang Nai (姚光鼐),
Divisional Officer of the West Gate Division, Chinese Police
Bureau, called at this office and discussed with Chief Inspector
Ross and the undersigned measures for a solution of the strike
in the Kung Yih Cotton Mill.
Although Mr. Yao at first denied having had anything
to do with the strike, he was gradually induced to speak and
began to realize his responsibility.
He stated that he knew the lawyer named Chow, now
entrusted by the Chung Nyi Sen Society (忠義社) to look
after the strike, and he would use his influence through Chow
to induce the strikers to come to terms without further delay.
He produced a paper containing the six demands of the workers
mentioned in Report of Gordon Road dated February 22, 1937,
and expressed the following opinions:-
Referring to No.1 demand that the seven No.1 men who
had retired be paid their compensation and their superannuation
fund in a lump sum, Mr. Yao said this demand must be complied
with as payment in instalments would not satisfy the workers.
Referring to the No.2 demand that all the discharged
workers be allowed to return to work, Mr. Yao said that if this
demand cannot be granted they should be paid six months wages
as compensation.
Mr. Yao was informed that the management would
probably agree to reinstate all the workers with the exception
of the 4 head women. As regards the six months wages as
compensation, the management would probably consider the issue
of compensation according to the length of service. It would
be unreasonable to issue six months pay to a worker who had

制作及转呈人：谭绍良督察长。

2月23日下午12点15分，中国警察局西区分局局长姚光鼐（Yao Kwang Nai）
来到本办公室，与罗斯首席督察（Chief Inspector Ross）及本人讨论了
解决公益棉纺厂罢工的方案。
虽然姚先生起初否认与罢工有任何关系，但经过逐步引导，他开始开口，
并逐渐意识到自己的责任。
他表示认识周律师，该律师目前受忠义社（Chung Nyi Sen Society）委托
处理罢工事宜，他将通过周律师施加影响，促使罢工者尽快达成和解。
他出示了一份文件，其中列出了1937年2月22日戈登路报告中提到的工人的六项要求，
并表达了以下意见：-
关于第一项要求，即一次性支付七名已退休的一号男工的赔偿金及其养老金基金，
姚先生说必须满足这一要求，因为分期付款无法令工人满意。
关于第二项要求，即允许所有被解雇的工人复工，姚先生说，如果这一
要求无法得到满足，则应支付六个月工资作为补偿。
有人告知姚先生，厂方可能会同意除四名女领班外，让所有工人复职。至于
六个月工资的补偿，厂方可能会根据工龄长短来考虑补偿问题。向仅工作了一两天的工人发放六个月工资是不合理的。

（印：RECD 23 FEB 10:30 SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE）

Date February 22, 1937.

Subject The Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road - strike situation.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I.

At 4 p.m. 21/2/37 a notice was posted outside
the mill gate by the management of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill,
150 Robison Road, instructing all workers to resume work. A
translation reads as follows:-

"Through the mediation of the Bureau of Social
Affairs, the misunderstanding which has arisen
out of the activities of a few dismissed em-
ployees, has been removed and the operations of
the mill will be resumed from the 22nd inst.
It is hoped that all workers will resume work as
usual."

When the mill was re-opened at 5.30 a.m. February
22, only some 170 workers out of about 1,700 hands reported
for work. Pickets sent out by the strikers were very active
at the undermentioned approaches to the mill, and prevented
workers from entering:-

1. Brenan Piece;
2. Siau Moh Jao, Jessfield Road near Kinnear Road;
3. Connaught Road near the China General Bus Coy's
Office;
4. Brenan Road near Edinburgh Road.

Enquiries show that through the mediation of Mr.
Tsang of the Bureau of Social Affairs, the management, in answer
to the demands of the strikers, made further concessions which
are as follows:-

1/. That the compensation of boys who had been dis-
charged to be increased from $5.00 and $6.00 to $8.00.
2/. That the boy chiefs who were granted to two
months' pay compensation, to be granted to 2½ months' pay.

1937年2月21日下午4时，罗宾森路150号公益纱厂管理层在厂门外张贴告示，指示所有工人复工。译文如下：

“经社会局调解，因少数被解雇员工之活动而产生的误会已消除，本厂将于本月22日起恢复运营。望全体工人照常复工。”

2月22日上午5时30分工厂重新开工时，约1,700名工人中仅有约170人到岗。罢工者派出的纠察队在下列通往工厂的路口非常活跃，并阻止工人进入：

3. 康纳脱路（Connaught Road）近中国通用汽车公司办事处处；
4. 白伦路（Brenan Road）近爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）处。

经查，经社会局曾先生调解，资方针对罢工者的要求作出了进一步让步，具体如下：

1. 被解雇童工的补偿金从5.00元和6.00元增加至8.00元。
2. 原获两个月工资补偿的童工领班，现改为给予两个半月工资。

Subject Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road - strike continues.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I.

At 11.30 a.m. February 20, 1937 the management of the
Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road gave the following reply
through the medium of Mr. Tsang Tsao Jang, representative of the
Bureau of Social Affairs, to the demands submitted by the
strikers:-

1. That the demand of reinstatement of all discharged
workers was not accepted;

2. That the demand to pay off all newly engaged employees
was not accepted;

3. That the seven discharged foremen will each be given
a retiring gratuity equivalent to four months' wages, and the
payment will be made in a lump sum one month after the resumption
of work. The superanuation of these workers will be issued after
six months' time from date;

4. That the fourteen boy overseers will be given two
months' pay as compensation instead of one month as originally
decided;

5. That among the discharged boy workers, the old ones
each
will be paid $6 each, whilst the remaining ones $5/instead of
$4 each as originally decided upon.

A report has been received to the effect that one Wong
Tsoh Ping, Standing Committee Member of the 3rd District Spinning
Union, No.10 Ying Sih Lee, Pootaq Road, has been trying to
persuade the strikers to join this union, in order to gain control
of the strike movement.

The strikers have not yet joined the union but are wait-
ing at the Union office for the reply to their demands.

Subject Strike in the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, O.O.L.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Sau-chien Forwarded by J. Boyne D S I

At 5.30 a.m. 18.2.37, 174 of the 300 female workers of
the 300 female workers of the spinning department of the Kung Yih
Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, failed to put in an appearance
without giving any reason and, as a result, the department was
closed down. The other departments were closed down by the
management at 6 p.m. 18.2.37 owing to shortage of cotton yarn.
A total of about 1,700 hands was thus affected.

At 2 p.m. 19.2.37 the following demands were presented
to the Mill management by the strikers through the medium of
Mr. Tsang Taoo Jang (张道江) of the Bureau of Social Affairs:-
(1). That the 7 discharged foremen each be given a
retiring gratuity equivalent to four months' wages in addition
to their superanuation and the payment be made in a lump sum
instead of by instalments.
(2). That the other workers discharged after the 8.2.37
be reinstated.
(3). That in case the second demand is not granted,
these ex-workers will each be given a retiring gratuity equivalent
to 10 months' wages.
(4). That assurance be given that no further workers
will be discharged in future.
(5). That all newly engaged employees be paid off.
(6). That all workers' wages be paid for the period of
strike.

Enquiries show that the sudden absence of the female
workers from work on 18.2.37 was believed to be due to the
activities of certain agitators who, according to information
received, sent out pickets to prevent the workers from entering
the mill in the early morning of 18.2.37.

1937年2月18日上午5时30分，罗宾森路150号公益纱厂细纱间300名女工中的174人无故未到岗，导致该部门停工。由于棉纱短缺，管理层于1937年2月18日下午6时关闭了其他部门。总计约1,700名工人受到影响。

1937年2月19日下午2时，罢工者通过社会局张道江先生向厂方提出以下要求：
(1). 七名被解雇领班除养老金外，每人另获相当于四个月工资的退休金，并一次性支付而非分期支付。
(2). 1937年2月8日后被解雇的其他工人予以复职。
(3). 若第二项要求未获批准，这些前工人每人将获得相当于十个月工资的退休金。
(4). 保证今后不再解雇工人。
(5). 遣散所有新雇佣的员工。
(6). 支付罢工期间所有工人的工资。

经查，1937年2月18日女工突然缺勤被认为是一些煽动者活动所致，据收到的消息，这些人于1937年2月18日清晨派出纠察队阻止工人进入工厂。

Kung Yih Cotton Mill - strike of workers
X The No.1 and 2 forewomen and some 174 of the 300
female workers of the Spinning Department of the Kung Yih
Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, failed to put in an appearance

is expected that the Winding and Reeling Departments will
be compelled to suspend operation later in the day owing
to a shortage of yarn in consequence of the closing of the
Spinning Department.

THE SITUATION IN KUNG YIH COTTON MILL

The strikers of the Kung Yih ( 公益 ) Cotton
Mill, No.150 Robison Road, held a meeting on the night of
February 14.
At 10 a.m. February 15, 14 representatives were
appointed by the strikers to submit an appeal to the local
Tangpu, the Bureau of Social Affairs and the General Labour
Union demanding:-
(1) The payment of a retiring gratuity equivalent to
six months' pay to each discharged foremen and worker in
accordance with the regulations governing the discharge
of foremen.
(2) In case the first demand is not granted, the
discharged foremen and workers be reinstated.
(3) The dismissal of the engineer Zing Tuh Min (秦佐明).

公益纱厂的局势

位于罗宾森路150号的公益（Kung Yih）纱厂的罢工者于2月14日晚举行了一次会议。
1937年2月15日上午10时，罢工者推选了14名代表，向当地塘浦（Tangpu，音译）、社会局和总工会提交请愿书，要求：-
(1) 按照管理解雇领班的规定，向每位被解雇的领班和工人支付相当于六个月工资的退休遣散费。
(2) 如果第一项要求未获批准，则复职被解雇的领班和工人。
(3) 解雇工程师秦佐明 (Zing Tuh Min)。

Subject Kung Yih Cotton Mill - Unrest among dismissed boys.
Made by D.I. Sih Tee-liang Forwarded by J. Bayne C.S.S.

The deposit money equivalent to nine days' wages
which was deducted from each worker or foremen at the beginning
of their service with the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, was refunded
at 2 p.m. February 10 to the dismissed hands - 7 foremen and
220 boys - through the foremen.

At 10 a.m. February 14, four No.1 boys called upon
the management of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill and requested that
a retiring gratuity equivalent to 6 months wages be issued to
them. The management however consented to fix the sum of
gratuity at one month's wages instead of half month as
previously announced. The callers were not satisfied with
the concession and subsequently withdrew.

It is learned that the fourteen No.1 boys who acted
as overseers among the "boys" held a conference in the house
of one named Lao Liu (老劉), an ex-worker of the Kung Yih
Mill, at 11 Tsih Teh Fang, Brenan Road, O.O.L. at 3 p.m.
February 14, 2nd and decided to proceed to the Bureau of Social Affairs
and the local Tangpu on February 15 and appeal for assistance
in securing a retiring gratuity equivalent to six months'
wages.

Some unrest also exists among the boys who are
agitating for an increase in the sum of retiring gratuity,
which according to the announcement of the management will be
$4 each.

制作人 侦探督察 Sih Tee-liang 转发人 J. Bayne C.S.S.

公益纱厂在工人或领班入职之初扣除的相当于九天工资的押金，已于2月10日下午2时通过领班退还给被解雇的人员——7名领班和220名童工。

2月14日上午10时，四名一号童工拜访了公益纱厂管理层，要求向他们发放相当于六个月工资的退休遣散费。然而，管理层同意将遣散费金额定为一个月工资，而非此前宣布的半个月工资。来访者对这一让步不满意，随后离去。

据悉，在“童工”中担任监工的十四名一号童工于2月14日下午3时在布伦南路（Brenan Road）芝德坊11号的前公益纱厂工人老刘 (Lao Liu) 家中召开会议，并决定于2月15日前往社会局和当地塘浦（Tangpu，音译），请求协助争取相当于六个月工资的退休遣散费。

在那些鼓动增加退休遣散费金额的童工中也存在一定程度的不安情绪，根据管理层的公告，该金额将为每人4美元。

Subject Mutual Aid Association - Activities among workers
of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, O.O.L.
Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by [Signature] D.S.I

(左侧边注：See also D.7599/36)

On December 15, 1936, seven employees of the Kung
Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, O.O.L., received letters
purporting to have emanated from the Shanghai Spinners' and
Weavers' Mutual Aid Association taxing them with not having
attended a meeting of departmental foremen convened by the
Association. The manager of the mill, Mr. Davis, had
previous information that the workers had held a meeting in
Chapel on December 14. Therefore, it was presumed that
trouble was in the making, although there was no definite
sign of unrest and no grievances had been expressed.
Rumours are afoot, however, that a strike may be declared,
and that a labour union is being formed. The appointment
of a new labour contractor, Mr. Zing Tuh Fong caused some
uneasiness during the past month but the fact that no
changes have been made in the staff and Mr. Zing has given
an assurance that none are intended has done much to remove
the uneasiness. Again, the management has recently granted
an increase of 5% in pay to the workers so there appears to
be no legitimate grievance.

the latest information indicates that this is the extent of
their immediate activities. The meeting mentioned by Mr. Davis
is presumably the one convened by the Mutual Aid Association
in the Ping Ming Tsung, Chung San Road, Chapel (Vide General
Report dated December 22, 1936).

主题：互助会——罗宾森路150号（老闸捕房辖区）公益纱厂工人中的活动
由 D.S. McKeown 撰写，经由 [签名] D.S.I 转呈

(左侧边注：另见 D.7599/36)

1936年12月15日，位于老闸捕房辖区罗宾森路150号的公益纱厂（Kung Yih Cotton Mill）七名雇员收到信件，声称来自上海纺织业互助会，指责他们未参加由该会召集的部门领班会议。该厂经理戴维斯先生（Mr. Davis）此前已获悉，工人们于12月14日在教堂举行了一次会议。因此，人们推测麻烦正在酝酿之中，尽管当时并没有明确的不安迹象，也没有表达任何不满。然而，有谣言称可能会宣布罢工，并且正在组建工会。新任劳工包工头辛图芳先生（Mr. Zing Tuh Fong，音译）的任命在过去一个月引起了一些不安，但由于员工队伍未发生变动，且辛先生保证无意进行变动，这在很大程度上消除了不安情绪。此外，管理层最近给予工人5%的加薪，因此似乎不存在正当的不满理由。

位于康纳路附近的金士杜庙街44号（King Sg Doo Miau Ka，音译）的互助会发起者正竭尽全力招募纱厂工人入会，但最新信息显示，这就是他们目前活动的全部范围。戴维斯先生提到的会议据推测是互助会在中山路平明总社教堂召集的会议（参见1936年12月22日的综合报告）。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JUNE 4, 1987

Mill Workers
"Go Slow" To
Get Demands

Six Riot Vans Called
From Two Stations To
Kung Yue Plant

A brief period of excitement was experienced at the Kung Yue Cotton Mill on Robisou Road at noon yesterday when several riot vans, four from the Gordon Road Police Station and two from the Zauka-doo District Bureau of Police, were rushed to the mill in response to request from the management.

The call for riot vans was made when more than 2,000 workers, both men and women, suddenly resorted to a "go-slow" strike to accelerate their demands for higher wages and better treatment presented by them during the strike some time ago.

Policemen from the Gordon Road Police Station who rushed to the mill aboard four riot vans later arrested 16 of the workers. The arrested workers were subsequently handed over to the police from the Zaukadoo District Bureau for questioning and detention.

The riot vans were withdrawn from the scene at 1 o'clock yesterday afternoon when the workers agreed to resume their duties.

“怠工”以

六辆防暴车从
两个警局调往
公裕工厂

昨天中午，罗宾森路的公裕纱厂（Kung Yue Cotton Mill，即公益纱厂）经历了一段短暂的骚动，应管理层请求，数辆防暴车紧急赶往该厂，其中四辆来自戈登路警察局，两辆来自曹家渡区警察局。

当两千多名男女工人突然采取“怠工”罢工，以加速实现他们在前次罢工期间提出的提高工资和改善待遇的要求时，发出了调用防暴车的请求。

乘坐四辆防暴车赶至该厂的戈登路警察局警察随后逮捕了16名工人。被捕工人随后被移交给曹家渡区警察局警察进行讯问和拘留。

昨天下午1点，当工人同意恢复工作时，防暴车撤离了现场。

Registration of workers to be employed at the
Kung Yik Cotton Mill, which commenced yesterday, May 10,
continues.

of Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd., the local Tangpu, Bureau

E SHANGHAI TIMES. SATURDAY, MAY 15, 1937

Kung Yik
Mill Now
Re-opened
60 Workers Dismissed;
Wage Increase Of 5
Cents Per Day

After several weeks agitation during which the management was forced to close business and to declare a lockout, workers of the Kung Yik (Ewo) Cotton Mill, a British mill in Robison Road, returned to work yesterday as a result of mediatory efforts made by officials of the Bureau of Social Affairs.

According to a Chinese news agency report the workers have agreed that 60 of their number will be dismissed after obtaining retiring gratuities. Those dismissed workers, who have worked for one year for the mill are each entitled to get an extra month's wage as gratuity, which will be proportionately increased in case they have worked for a longer period. All workers returning to work will have their daily wage increased by five cents.

It will be recalled that the workers had been agitating for better treatment for some months. On April 1, they declared a strike, alleging that their management had failed to accept their demands. A serious riot broke out just after the strike was called. More than 10 workers were injured in the riot. The management later decided to effect a lockout and to close the mill. The workers became desperate. They tried several times to go to Nanking to petition for help, after their management had failed to send representatives to official mediation meetings.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年5月15日，星期六

公怡
纱厂现已
重新开工
60名工人被解雇；
每日工资增加
5分钱

经过数周的动荡，期间资方被迫停业并宣布闭厂，位于罗宾森路的英商公怡（怡和）纱厂工人在社会局官员的调解努力下，于昨日复工。

据一家中文通讯社报道，工人们已同意在获得遣散费后解雇其中的60人。那些在该厂工作满一年的被解雇工人，每人有权获得相当于一个月工资的额外遣散费，若工作年限更长，则按比例增加。所有复工工人的日工资将增加五分钱。

回顾此前，工人们数月来一直为争取更好待遇而奔走。4月1日，他们宣布罢工，声称资方拒绝接受他们的要求。罢工发起后不久便爆发了严重骚乱。骚乱中有十多名工人受伤。资方随后决定实行闭厂并关闭纱厂。工人们陷入绝望。在资方未派代表参加官方调解会议后，他们多次试图前往南京请愿求助。

April 22, 1937. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:-

KUNG YIH COTTON MILL STRIKE SITUATION

The recent mediation by the Bureau of
Social Affairs for the settlement of the labour strike in
the Kung Yih Cotton Mill, 150 Robison Road, O.O.L., produced
no result owing to the absence of representatives from
the employers.

Owing to the wet weather, the meeting
of workers scheduled to be held at 1 p.m. yesterday in
the compound of the Kan Kung Primary School ( 幹 公 小 學 ) did
not take place. The meeting will be held this afternoon
to discuss measures for proceeding with the matter and for
election of representatives to submit appeals to Nanking.

A notice has been issued by the cotton mill
intimating that all workers be re-registered, but this
has been refused by the workers during the period of
mediation.

It is learnt that the Bureau of Social
Affairs will refer the dispute for arbitration.

Date 21 / 4 / 37.
April 21, 1937.

NIPPO

DISPUTE BETWEEN LABOUR AND CAPITAL IN SHANGHAI

Inspite of the suppressive
action adopted by the Shanghai City Government and the
Kuomintang, labour strikes in Shanghai are spreading.
It is not known yet whether these strikes are due to the
rising cost of living or to outside influence. However
the strikers are very well organized and they are believed
to be receiving instructions from certain outside persons.

Changing it s policy of appealing
to the masses by using communistic slogans, as a result of
the changed political situation in China, the Chinese
communist party is believed to be extending its activities
to the important industrial organizations in Shanghai.

It is natural for the Chinese
communist party, which regards itself as a political party,
to try to curry favour with industrial labourers in a
place like Shanghai where the industries are so important.
We cannot regard the present industrial labour trouble
as a matter concerning the Chinese only, for the reason
that the Japanese have much capital invested in cotton
mills in Shanghai and the North. If the trouble extends
to the Japanese cotton mills it will be a serious problem
which will require out attention. All Powers should
co-operate to suppress such trouble.

1937年4月21日。

《日日新闻》

上海的劳资纠纷

尽管上海市政府和国民党采取了镇压行动，上海的罢工仍在蔓延。目前尚不清楚这些罢工是由于生活成本上升还是受外部影响所致。然而，罢工者组织严密，据信他们正接受某些外部人士的指示。

鉴于中国政治局势的变化，中国共产党改变了以往利用共产主义口号动员群众的政策，据信其活动正扩展至上海的重要工业组织。

对于一个自视为政党的中国共产党来说，在上海这样工业至关重要的地方，试图讨好产业工人是自然而然的。我们不能将当前的产业劳工纠纷仅视为与中国有关的事务，因为日本在上海及华北的纱厂投入了大量资本。如果纠纷蔓延至日资纱厂，将成为一个需要我们关注的严重问题。各国应合作镇压此类动乱。

April 21, 1937. Afternoon Translation

Chin Pao (今報), a mosquito newspaper, publishes the following article :-

A TRIVIAL AFFAIR

Appearing before Judge Chu Tsoo-tsoh(朱楚舸) of the Shanghai Second Special District Court on a charge of having stolen a piece of copper in the afternoon of April 12, one Chang Yu-san(張裕山), aged 43, native of Shantung, pleaded guilty to the charge and said: "I know it is a bad thing to steal, but I was compelled to do it because of hunger. I risked the danger of stealing the piece of copper with the intention of later selling it to enable me to buy some cakes to satisfy my hunger."
"Can you not work?" asked the Judge of the prisoner in the dock.
"I am homeless in Shanghai. My eyes are bad and I cannot find any work," replied the prisoner.
The Judge again asked, "Can you make a living by begging if you are released?"
The prisoner replied, "It is not an easy thing to beg for alms in Shanghai. I have been begging for many days without much success. I have no other alternative but to drown myself if your Honour releases me."
It is the general opinion of the public that stealing is to be detested and that whenever an individual is at his wit's end to earn a living, he can turn into a beggar and should refrain from committing theft. Some thieves willingly commit thefts, but most of them are forced to steal because they have been unsuccessful at begging. Frankly speaking, the Chinese and Settlement authorities of Shanghai do not permit begging on the streets by the poor because in their eyes it impairs the good appearance of the district. Was not a beggar sleeping on a bridge "thrown" into a creek? Are not the tramps on the streets arrested and put into vans to be driven out of the prosperous metropolis?

小报《今报》刊登了以下文章：

一件小事

4月12日下午，43岁的山东籍男子张裕山因被控盗窃一块铜而出庭受审，他在上海第二特区地方法院朱楚舸法官面前认罪，并称：“我知道偷窃是坏事，但因饥饿所迫才这样做。我冒着危险偷这块铜，打算日后卖掉买些糕点充饥。”
法官问被告：“你难道不能工作吗？”
囚犯回答说：“我在上海无家可归。我眼睛不好，找不到工作。”
法官又问：“如果释放你，你能靠乞讨为生吗？”
囚犯回答说：“在上海乞讨并非易事。我已乞讨多日，收获甚微。如果大人释放我，我别无选择，只能投水自尽。”
公众普遍认为，偷窃令人憎恶，当个人生计陷入绝境时，可以沦为乞丐，但不应行窃。有些小偷是自愿行窃，但大多数是因为乞讨不成而被迫偷窃。坦率地说，上海的中外当局不允许穷人在街头乞讨，因为在他们看来，这有损该地区的良好观感。难道没有睡在桥上的乞丐被“扔”进小河里吗？街头的流浪汉难道不是被捕后装上货车，被驱逐出这座繁华的大都市吗？

KUNG YIK TROUBLE IN
LIMELIGHT AGAIN

Workers Said Angry On
Outcome Of Parley,
With Company

workers of the suspended Kung
Yik (Ewo) Cotton Mill, Robison
Road, and its affiliated mills in
Yangtzepoo would assume serious

by their management, declared
that they would hold a meeting
this afternoon in Brenan Road in
order to elect representatives who
would refer their grievances to the
Ministry of Industry in Nanking.
Officials of the Bureau of Social
Affairs tried to effect a compro-
mise yesterday by holding a media-
tion meeting at which the manage-
ment was not represented. The pre-
siding official, Mr. Wang Hsieh-
ching, declared that official media-
tion had failed and that the matter
should be referred to an arbitra-
tion committee in accordance with
the revised regulations.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, APRIL 17, 1937

Women Workers Of Kung
Yik Dispersed By Police

Group Of 600 Form Procession To March To Civic
Centre; Settlement Riot Squad Stands By
Near Mill Awaiting Eventualities

With a large number of them showing discontent with the strike and expressing their wish to return to work, about 600 female workers of the Kung Yik (Ewo) Cotton Mill, 150, Robison Road, which has been closed since April 1, gathered for a mass meeting yesterday morning on the playground of the Kang Kung Primary School on Brenan Road.

Following a short meeting the women formed a procession with the intention of marching to the Civic Centre in order to request the Bureau of Social Affairs to mediate with the management on their behalf Settlement authorities feared that the women might decide to march on the factory and cause damage there and immediately the Reserve Unit was rushed to the scene.

The workers, however, marched into Chinese territory, only to have their procession broken up by the Chinese Police. The rain that came down later completely dispersed them.

After the workers, some 3,000 in number went on strike on April 1 the management declared a lock-out and recently posted a notice that new hands would be hired.

Silk Situation

The strike wave among Chinese silk filatures still continued yesterday with workers of one filature returning to work, and those of another calling a general strike. Under the supervision of officials from the Bureau of Social Affairs the striking workers of the Ching Shing Silk Weaving Factory, Pingliang Road returned to work yesterday morning Because their management did not allow a 10 per cent. increase in wages as ordered by the Bureau workers of the Fu Ching Silk Filature, Brenan Road, called a strike yesterday.

Representatives of workers of the 10 factories of the Mayar Silk Works all of which were recently closed because of lack of refined silk resulting from the strike called by the No. 1 factory of the company in Nantao, went to the Bureau to petition for help. They insisted that their management should increase their wages by 10 per cent., as was mentioned in a Bureau order, to which their management took exception. The matter has been referred to the Shanghai City Government for a final settlement.

公益纱厂女工被警察驱散

约600人组成队伍拟前往市中心；租界防暴队驻守工厂附近以待事态发展

由于许多女工对罢工表示不满并表达复工意愿，位于罗宾森路150号、自4月1日起停工的公益（怡和）纱厂约600名女工，于昨日上午在勃伦南路康工小学的操场上集会。

简短会议后，女工们组成游行队伍，意图前往市中心，请求社会局代表她们与资方进行调解。租界当局担心女工可能会决定向工厂进发并造成破坏，随即调派后备队赶赴现场。

然而，工人们行进至华界 territory，其游行队伍被中国警察驱散。随后降下的雨水将她们彻底冲散。

自4月1日约3000名工人罢工后，资方宣布闭厂，并于近日张贴告示称将雇佣新工人。

丝绸业局势

昨日，中国丝厂的罢工浪潮仍在持续，一家丝厂的工人复工，另一家丝厂的工人则发动总罢工。在社会局官员的监督下，平凉路景兴丝织厂的罢工工人于昨日上午复工。由于资方未按社会局命令允许增加10%的工资，勃伦南路福庆丝厂的工人于昨日举行罢工。

美亚绸厂旗下10家工厂的工人代表前往社会局请愿求助，这些工厂近期均因该公司位于南市的一厂发起罢工导致熟丝短缺而关闭。他们坚持要求资方按照社会局命令所述增加10%的工资，但资方对此提出异议。此事已提交上海市政府作最终裁决。

Kung Yih Cotton Mill (British) - Strike of workers

At 5.45 a. m. April 1, approximately 3,000 day and night shift workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill (British), 150 Robison Road, O.C.I., declared a strike and commenced to destroy machinery and equipment in an endeavour to force the management to accede to the following demands :-

1. That the new staff engaged by the management be discharged, and vacancies such as "engineers" be filled by experienced workers at present employed.

2. That the management make an assurance that no worker be dismissed without reasonable cause.

3. That when a worker is on leave and a substitute is engaged, full pay for the substitute be paid by the management.

4. That workers be given extra pay for increase in work.

5. That the management establish a club, to be controlled by workers, for the benefit of the workers.

6. That the rice allowance be restored, and the 10% deduction in pay effected last year be abolished.

7. That wages be paid for the period of the recent strike.

8. That an agreement between the management and the workers be signed if the above demands are accepted by the management.

Following the refusal of the employees to leave the mill premises, a clash took place between the workers and the Municipal Police who eventually succeeded in ejecting the strikers. During the ensuing melee a number of workers were injured. No arrests were made.

4月1日上午5时45分，位于老闸捕房辖区罗便臣道150号的英商公益纱厂约3000名日班和夜班工人宣布罢工，并开始破坏机器设备，试图迫使管理层接受以下要求：-

1. 解雇管理层新聘用的职员，并由目前受雇的有经验工人填补“工程师”等空缺职位。

2. 管理层保证不得无故解雇任何工人。

3. 当工人请假并雇用替工时，替工的全额工资应由管理层支付。

4. 工作量增加应给予工人额外报酬。

5. 管理层应建立一个由工人控制、为工人谋福利的俱乐部。

6. 恢复米贴，并废除去年实施的10%扣薪规定。

7. 支付最近罢工期间的工资。

8. 如果管理层接受上述要求，应与工人签署协议。

由于雇员拒绝离开工厂厂区，工人与公共租界巡捕发生冲突，巡捕最终成功将罢工者驱逐。在随后的混战中，多名工人受伤。无人被捕。

杂项

当地党部宴请吴铁城市长和孔祥熙博士

在当地党部、淞沪警备司令部及其他官方和公共团体的主持下，为吴铁城市长、孔祥熙博士以及代理市长俞鸿钧先生举行午宴

April 2, 1937. / Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated April 1 and other local newspapers :-

CLASH AT KUNG YIH COTTON MILL

As a protest against the refusal by their management to comply with their demands for better treatment, the entire body of the workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill (公益紗廠), a British concern, at No. 150 Robison Road, O.O.L., went on strike at 6 a.m. April 1. The Gordon Road Police Station was notified and more than 20 detectives and uniformed policemen were detailed to the mill to maintain order.

(秦德芳), Just at the time when Mr. Zing Tuh Fang, an engineer of the mill, was in conversation with the police officials, the workers on the upper floor of the mill opened the window to look downstairs, and in so doing a piece of wood attached to the window became loosened and dropped upon one of the policemen downstairs. The police official at once rushed upstairs and demanded from the workers an explanation.

Noticing the presence of police officials, the workers became excited and all rushed downstairs. The policemen downstairs, upon learning of this, at once went upstairs and assaulted with batons the workers they met. A clash thus ensued which resulted in great disorder in the mill.

Consequently, the Gordon Road Police Station was notified by telephone by the detectives, and more than 30 additional Chinese and foreign policemen were sent to the scene of trouble in two riot vans, while at the same time more than 80 policemen in four riot vans were detailed from the Reserve Unit. Upon noticing the presence of so many police officers, the workers became more excited.

Upon learning of the trouble, a party of police was detailed from the Gordon Road Sub-Station and the Detective Squad of the Police Bureau, but as they were refused admittance into the mill, they were unable to render protection. Later, more than 80 members of the S.V.C. arrived at the scene in four vans, but they were soon withdrawn as the workers had already been dispersed.

During the clash between the Municipal Police and the workers, 19 workers were injured in the head. 11 of them who sustained serious injuries were conveyed to the Chung San Hospital, while the remainder were sent to the Lester Hospital for treatment.

Following their ejection from the mill, the workers held an urgent meeting at 5 p.m. yesterday at House No. 7 Min Sun Lee (民新里) alleyway off Brenan Road at which it was resolved that the local Tangpu and Government authorities be notified of the circumstances of the incident and be requested to open negotiations. During the meeting, representatives were appointed to make appeals to the local Party and Government organs in the afternoon.

4月1日的《华美晚报》及其他本地报纸：-

公益纱厂冲突

为抗议管理层拒绝满足其改善待遇的要求，位于老闸捕房辖区罗便臣道150号的英商企业公益纱厂全体工人于4月1日上午6时罢工。戈登路捕房接到通知，并派遣20多名便衣侦探和制服警察前往该厂维持秩序。

(秦德芳)，就在该厂工程师秦德芳先生与警方官员交谈时，工厂楼上的工人打开窗户向下看，在此过程中，附着在窗户上的一块木板松动，掉落在楼下的一名警察身上。该警官立即冲上楼，要求工人作出解释。

工人们注意到警方官员的存在，情绪激动，全部冲下楼。楼下的警察得知此事后，立即上楼，用警棍殴打遇到的工人。由此引发冲突，导致工厂内大乱。

因此，侦探通过电话通知戈登路捕房，另外30多名中外警察乘坐两辆防暴车被派往出事现场，同时从后备队抽调80多名警察乘坐四辆防暴车前往。工人们看到如此多的警察在场，情绪更加激动。

得知骚乱情况后，戈登路分巡捕房和警务处侦探股派遣了一队警察，但由于被拒绝进入工厂，他们无法提供保护。后来，80多名上海义勇军（S.V.C.）成员乘坐四辆卡车抵达现场，但由于工人已经散去，他们很快撤离。

在公共租界巡捕与工人的冲突中，19名工人头部受伤。其中11名重伤者被送往中山医院，其余人员被送往莱斯脱医院接受治疗。

被逐出厂后，工人们于昨日下午5时在勃伦安路民新里7号举行紧急会议，决定将事件情况通知当地党部和政府当局，并请求开启谈判。会议期间，指派代表于下午向当地党和政府机关提出申诉。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, APRIL 2, 1937

Many Injured In Rioting
At Kung Yik Cotton Mill;
Stay-In Strike Declared

Reserve Unit Called Out To Evict 3,000 Day And
Night Hands; Detachment Of Russian Regt.
On Scene As More Trouble Expected

ONLY $1,000 DAMAGE ESTIMATED;
LOCK-OUT IS DECLARED

Almost 50 workers were injured, 11 of them sustaining fairly serious injuries. Many window panes were broken and machinery damaged in a riot which broke out at the Kung Yik Cotton Mill, one of the Ewo group, at 150 Robison Road, early yesterday morning. The Reserve Unit of the Shanghai Municipal Police had to be called out to reinforce the officers of Gordon Road Police Station in evicting 3,000 workers of the day and night shift from the factory premises. The rioting was expected to reach serious proportions and two detachments of the Russian Regiment, S.V.C., were rushed to the scene and stood by on Robison Road awaiting eventualities.

The workers were finally evicted and a lock-out was declared by the management. A check estimated that only about $1,000 worth of property damage was done. A large number of window panes were broken and slight damage was done to several of the looms. The situation was quiet last night, a small detachment of police standing guard at the factory. No demands had been submitted by the workers.

The trouble started shortly before 6 o'clock when the 1,500 night shift workers were scheduled to come off work and the same number of day shift hands had come to replace them. When the time came for the change of shifts, the night shift workers refused to leave the premises, while the day shift hands all trooped into the factory.

A rather curious situation arose, part of the workers wanting to work, while the other part refused to let them do so. Mediation was immediately commenced and a call was put through to Gordon Road Police Station, a large squad of police under Inspector R. C. Hall immediately turning out.

Refuse To Leave

The workers were finally given the alternative of continuing to work or leaving the factory. They refused to do either and then a call for reinforcements was put through and the Reserve Unit under Chief Inspector J. F. Lovell rushed to the scene in the two Red Marias. The two police vans drove into the factory compound and it was then that the rioting commenced, workers breaking window panes and throwing bobbins at the police and the van standing below. Minor damage was also done to several of the looms.

A party of police was then rushed through the back of the factory and the slow process of pushing the workers out commenced. Further difficulty arose when fights started inside the factory between different factions of workers. Some wanted to continue to work, while others ordered them to stop. Most of the 2,000 female workers wanted to continue to work, while the trouble was mostly carried on by the 400 odd coolies.

The general advance of the police to clear out the workers started at about 7 o'clock, and the factory premises and the compound were all cleared within half an hour. A number of workers were injured, not all by the police, but some in fighting among themselves. Eleven were rushed in ambulances to the Sacred Heart Hospital, while many others had their injuries attended to by ambulance men on the spot.

Old Trouble

The rioting, the strike and the subsequent lock-out declared by the management date back to February 19, when a dispute arose between the management and the workers and, it is understood, was temporarily settled. The trouble yesterday, it is strongly believed, has been started by outside elements, instigated by the various male and female heads of groups, who lately have been deprived of a large amount of "squeeze" by the new system of wage payment devised by the management.

Previously the wage money was all paid to the foreman or forewoman, who paid off their group of workers. For about a month now the management has issued the wage money direct to the workers, with the result that the "squeeze" taken by the heads of groups is eliminated.

It has been stated that the workers went on strike in order to enforce a demand for an increase in wages. However, up to late yesterday afternoon the management of the factory had not received any formal demand.

Workers' Meeting

A meeting was called by the workers yesterday afternoon at which it was decided to petition the Bureau of Social Affairs to help them in mediating with the management and also to obtain medical fees for the injured men. It was also decided to maintain that the management should be held fully responsible for the riot and the damage resulting from it. They also decided to insist on being granted all the demands made on February 19, including one for an increase in wages.

It was learnt last night that the riotous workers decided to petition officials of the Bureau of Social Affairs to-day for assistance in settling their trouble. They claimed, at a meeting held last night, that they had presented eight demands to their management. The Bureau, it was further learnt, would try to mediate on Monday.

They demanded that besides the engineer who must be appointed by the mill management other officers of the mill should be ejected and old workers put in their place. They asked for guarantees against dismissal of workers, proportional increase of wages for more working hours, a club to be financed by the mill but managed by workers, restoration of last year's wages, which were reduced by 10 per cent., and payment of wages during the strike which they called on February 19.

（批：S-1 / 18/4 268 R. / 2/4）

《字林西报》，1937年4月2日，星期五

公益纱厂骚乱多人受伤；
宣布留厂罢工

出动后备队驱逐三千名日班和夜班工人；俄籍兵团分队到场，以防事态进一步恶化

估计损失仅1,000美元；资方宣布闭厂

近50名工人受伤，其中11人伤势较重。昨日清晨，位于罗宾森路150号、隶属于怡和集团的公益纱厂（Kung Yik Cotton Mill）发生骚乱，许多窗玻璃被砸碎，机器受损。上海公共租界工部局警务处不得不调派后备队，增援戈登路捕房的警员，将工厂内的3,000名日班和夜班工人驱逐出厂。鉴于骚乱可能升级，上海万国商团（S.V.C.）俄籍兵团的两个分队紧急赶赴现场，在罗宾森路待命以应对突发情况。

工人们最终被驱逐，资方随后宣布闭厂。经核查，估计财产损失仅约1,000美元。大量窗玻璃破碎，几台织布机受到轻微损坏。昨晚局势平静，一小队警察在工厂守卫。工人方面尚未提出任何要求。

冲突发生在早晨6点前不久，当时1,500名夜班工人预定下班，同等数量的日班工人前来接班。到了换班时间，夜班工人拒绝离开工厂，而日班工人则全部涌入厂内。

出现了一种相当奇特的局面：部分工人希望工作，而另一部分工人则阻止他们工作。调解工作立即展开，并致电戈登路捕房，由督察R. C. Hall率领的大批警员随即出动。

拒绝离开

工人们最终被给予继续工作或离开工厂的选择。他们两者均予拒绝，随后请求增援，由总督察J. F. Lovell率领的后备队乘坐两辆“红玛丽亚”警车（Red Marias）紧急赶赴现场。两辆警车驶入工厂大院，骚乱随即爆发，工人砸碎窗玻璃，并向警察及下方的警车投掷纱管。几台织布机也受到了轻微损坏。

随后，一队警察从工厂后方突入，开始缓慢地将工人推挤出厂。当工厂内部不同派系的工人之间发生斗殴时，困难进一步加剧。一些人希望继续工作，而另一些人则命令他们停止。2,000名女工中大多数人希望继续工作，而麻烦主要由400多名苦力挑起。

警察清理工人的全面行动大约在7点钟开始，工厂厂房和大院在半小时内全部清空。多名工人受伤，并非全由警察所致，有些是在互相斗殴中受伤。11人被救护车送往圣心医院（Sacred Heart Hospital），还有许多其他伤者在现场由救护人员进行了救治。

旧有纠纷

此次骚乱、罢工以及随后资方宣布的闭厂，可追溯至2月19日，当时资方与工人之间发生争端，据悉已暂时解决。人们强烈认为，昨天的麻烦是由外部势力挑起的，煽动者是各男女工头，由于资方设计了新的工资支付制度，这些工头最近失去了大量的“克扣”收入。

此前，工资全部支付给男工头或女工头，由他们向其管辖的工人群体发放。大约一个月来，资方直接向工人发放工资，结果是工头们的“克扣”被消除。

据称，工人罢工是为了强制要求增加工资。然而，直到昨天下午晚些时候，工厂管理层尚未收到任何正式的要求。

工人会议

工人们于昨天下午召开会议，决定向社会局请愿，请求协助与资方进行调解，并为受伤者争取医药费。会议还决定坚持认为资方应对骚乱及其造成的损害负全部责任。他们还决定坚持要求满足2月19日提出的所有要求，包括增加工资。

昨晚获悉，参与骚乱的工人决定今天向社会局官员请愿，寻求协助解决纠纷。他们在昨晚举行的会议上声称，已向资方提出了八项要求。进一步获悉，社会局将尝试在周一进行调解。

他们要求，除了必须由厂方任命的工程师外，还应罢免工厂的其他职员，并由老工人取而代之。他们要求提供保障，防止解雇工人；因工作时间延长而按比例增加工资；建立一个由工厂出资但由工人管理的俱乐部；恢复去年被削减10%的工资水平；并支付他们在2月19日号召罢工期间的工资。

（批注：S-1 / 18/4 268 R. / 2/4）

遵照此令，在总共1,700名工人中，有200名罢工者于今晨2月26日到岗上班。

据信，大量罢工者被部署在华界地区的纠察队阻止复工。

两家棉纺厂（英资）- 发现传单

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

FOH LUEN SILK FILATURE WORKERS ON STRIKE

The Foh Luen Silk Filature (福倫 ) on Tien Pao Road, Chapei, employs about 600 workers of both sexes.
As a protest against the rejection of their demands for better treatment and an increase of wages, the 600 operatives went on strike yesterday morning. Both the management and the strikers have submitted reports to the Bureau of Social Affairs and have asked for mediation.
It is understood that this morning the Bureau will detail officials to mediate in the dispute.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:

THE STRIKE OF KUNG YIH COTTON MILL WORKERS

In connection with the strike of workers of the Kung Yih Cotton Mill ( 公益 ), Robison Road, the representatives of workers of various departments yesterday afternoon held a meeting at which it was resolved that five representatives be appointed to request the Bureau of Social Affairs to mediate.
Yesterday the management posted up a notice advising the strikers to return to work, but none of the strikers reported for duty.

Star Daily News (明星日報 ) publishes the following comment :-

CRITICISM OF S.M.C.

In the past the authorities of the Foreign Settlements used to permit the showing of films derogatory to China, such as "Welcome Danger" and "Shanghai Express".
According to yesterday's papers, the Central Film Censorship Committee has published a notification stating that a film entitled "We Who Are About to Die" produced by the Peacock Motion Picture Corporation had been banned by the Shanghai Municipal Council.
This film deals with the life in gaol of a person who has been wrongfully imprisoned and is based on the actual experiences of an American named Lampson. A responsible official of the S.M.C. states that the picture is not suitable for exhibition in Shanghai as it is liable to induce prisoners to create trouble.
As a matter of fact, there is no chance for prisoners to see the picture. The S.M.C. is very cautious about prisoners, yet it has allowed films derogatory to China to be shown in the Settlement. This shows that the S.M.C. is afraid of trouble being created by prisoners, but is not afraid of the Chinese people. Are we Chinese inferior even to prisoners?

福伦丝厂工人罢工

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

公益纱厂工人罢工

关于罗宾森路公益纱厂（公益）工人罢工一事，各部门工人代表于昨天下午举行会议，决议推选五名代表请求社会局进行调解。
昨天，资方张贴告示，劝告罢工者复工，但无一名罢工者报到上班。

《明星日报》发表如下评论：

批评工部局

过去，租界当局允许放映诋毁中国的电影，如《欢迎危险》（Welcome Danger）和《上海快车》（Shanghai Express）。
据昨日报纸报道，中央电影检查委员会发布通知称，孔雀电影公司制作的名为《我们将死之人》（We Who Are About to Die）的电影已被上海公共租界工部局禁映。
该片讲述了一名被错误监禁者的狱中生活，基于一名叫Lampson的美国人的真实经历。工部局一位负责官员表示，该片不适合在上海放映，因为它可能诱发囚犯制造麻烦。
事实上，囚根本没有机会看到这部电影。工部局对囚犯非常谨慎，但却允许在租界内放映诋毁中国的电影。这表明工部局害怕囚犯制造麻烦，却不害怕中国人民。难道我们中国人还不如囚犯吗？

February 25, 1938. Morning Translation.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:-

THE STRIKE IN THE KUNG YIH COTTON MILL

Despite mediation by the local Tangpu and
other Government organs, the strike in the Kung Yih (公益)
Cotton Mill on Robison Road in the western district of
Shanghai remains unsettled.

With a view to preventing the dispute from
assuming serious proportions, the local Tangpu and the
Bureau of Social Affairs yesterday issued a joint notification
ordering the strikers to resume work pending a settlement
of the dispute.

The Spinning and Winding Department of the Sing
Yeu No.1 Mill which closed in the evening of February 17
following a strike of the night shift hands (Vide I.R.
18/2/37) resumed work on February 18.

Kung Yih Cotton Mill - strike continues

Owing to the suspension of operations by workers
in the Spinning Department and the subsequent shortage
of cotton yarn, the management of the Kung Yih Cotton
Mill closed down the other departments at 6 p.m. February
18. Some 1,700 hands were thus affected.

The situation remains unchanged this morning,
February 19, and although the strikers have not yet
submitted any demand to the management, their represent-
atives appealed to the Bureau of Social Affairs for
assistance on February 17 and 18 when the following
demands were expressed :-

1. That all the foremen and juvenile workers who have
been discharged be reinstated.

2. That, if the above mentioned demand is not accepted
by the management, a retiring gratuity equivalent
to 6 months' wages be issued to each of the dismissed
foremen and workers.

3. That engineer Zing Tuh-King (李德明) be dismissed.

A meeting will take place in the forenoon of
February 19, 1937, between representatives of the
strikers and a representative of the Bureau of Social
Affairs for the purpose of discussing the demands.

1. 复职所有被解雇的工头和童工。

Hung Shing Hosiery Factory - Agitation of Workers

The Hung Shing Hosiery Factory, a Chinese concern located at 221 Rue du Marche, which closed in December, 1936, for New Year holidays, re-opened on February 18th, when thirteen dismissed workers turned up and demanded re-instatement. This demand was supported by the 300 workers of the factory. The Management, however, rejected the demand, and declared a lockout on February 19th to counteract the agitation of the employees.

At 10 a.m. February 19th, ten Committee members of the 2nd District Knitting Workers' Union held a meeting in the Union Office, 25 Sien Sien Sz Loong, Nantao, when it was decided to refer the dispute existing in the Hung Shing Factory to the Chinese Authorities.

Labour

Sing Yeu No.1 Cotton Mill - strike of workers

At 11 a.m. February 17, approximately 100 day shift
operatives of the Spinning and Winding Departments of the
Sing Yeu No.1 Cotton Mill, No.37 West Soochow Road, stopped
work and demanded that the clerical staff who had been
discharged be re-instated and that a wage increase of 5
cents per day be granted. This movement was supported
by 300 night shift hands of the same department who
absented themselves from duty in the night of February 17/18.
The management refused to consider these demands and
threatened to dismiss those workers who were dissatisfied
with the present working conditions, whereupon the strikers
of the day shift returned to work unconditionally this
morning, February 18. It is expected that the night
shift strikers will resume work this evening.

Kung Yih Cotton Mill - strike of workers

The No.1 and 2 forewomen and some 174 of the 300
female workers of the Spinning Department of the Kung Yih
Cotton Mill, 150 Robinson Road, failed to put in an appearance
at 5.30 a.m. this morning, February 18, 1937, without giving
any reason. Owing to a lack of hands, this Department was
closed down, the 126 workers present being sent away.

Operations are being continued in other departments, but it
is expected that the Winding and Reeling Department will
be compelled to suspend operation later in the day owing
to a shortage of yarn in consequence of the closing of the
spinning Department.

纱厂罢工调解失败

昨日，对位于罗宾逊路的申裕和公益纱厂工人罢工的官方调解未取得明确结果。周日开始罢工的罢工工人仍坚持要求接受他们的所有要求。预计今天将继续进行进一步谈判。

申裕纱厂工人罢工是因为管理层最近解雇了一些职员。据报道，昨天管理层接受了罢工者提出的一些要求，包括向被解雇者支付十个月工资的要求。加薪百分之五的要求被驳回。

公益纱厂的劳工动荡是由最近几个部门工人被解雇引起的。愤怒的工人计划今天向中国当局请愿，要求复职被解雇的工人或给予六个月工资。他们还将要求解雇一名工程师。

February 16, 1937. | Afternoon Translations

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

LABOUR TROUBLE IN HSIN YUI COTTON MILL

As a protest against the dismissal of certain members of the staff by the management, the workers of the Hsin Yui (新裕) Cotton Mill, No.8 Robison Road, went on strike on the morning of February 14.
As no satisfactory reply was given by the management to the six demands submitted by the strikers, the workers on the morning of February 15 appointed nine representatives to submit an appeal to the local Tangpu, the Bureau of Social Affairs and the General Labour Union demanding:-
(1) The recognition of the Workers' Union as the representative of the workers.
(2) The restoration of operations.
(3) A reduction in the number of working days to four per week.
(4) A 5% increase in wages.
(5) The cessation of unreasonable discharges of workers.
(6) The maintenance of the present system of working.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

THE SITUATION IN KUNG YIH COTTON MILL

The strikers of the Kung Yih (公益) Cotton Mill, No.150 Robison Road, held a meeting on the night of February 14.
At 10 a.m. February 15, 14 representatives were appointed by the strikers to submit an appeal to the local Tangpu, the Bureau of Social Affairs and the General Labour Union demanding:-
(1) The payment of a retiring gratuity equivalent to six months' pay to each discharged foremen and worker in accordance with the regulations governing the discharge of foremen.
(2) In case the first demand is not granted, the discharged foremen and workers be reinstated.
(3) The dismissal of the engineer Zing Tuh Min (秦佐明).

Sin Wan Pao (Tientsin telegram):

COUNTERFEIT NOTES IN THE NORTH

Large numbers of counterfeit banknotes have appeared in Tientsin and Peiping. Many of the dens manufacturing these counterfeit notes were raided. These counterfeit notes are manufactured and uttered mostly by ronins.
On February 15, the Hopei-Chahar Political Council informed the Tientsin City Government to the effect that any person arrested for counterfeiting banknotes in future would be executed as a warning to others.

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

新裕纱厂的劳资纠纷

为抗议管理层解雇某些职员，位于罗宾逊路8号的新裕 (Hsin Yui) 纱厂工人于2月14日上午罢工。
由于管理层对罢工者提出的六项要求未给予满意答复，工人们于2月15日上午推选九名代表，向当地党部、社会局和总工会提交请愿书，要求：
(1) 承认工会为工人代表。
(2) 恢复生产。
(3) 将每周工作日减少至四天。
(4) 工资增加5%。
(5) 停止不合理地解雇工人。
(6) 维持现有的工作制度。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

公益纱厂的局势

位于罗宾逊路150号的公益 (Kung Yih) 纱厂罢工者于2月14日晚举行会议。
2月15日上午10时，罢工者推选14名代表，向当地党部、社会局和总工会提交请愿书，要求：
(1) 根据工头解雇规定，向每位被解雇的工头和工人支付相当于六个月工资的遣散费。
(2) 如果第一项要求未获批准，则复职被解雇的工头和工人。
(3) 解雇工程师秦佐明 (Zing Tuh Min)。

《新闻报》（天津电）：

北方出现假币

天津和北平出现大量假钞。许多制造这些假钞的窝点遭到突袭。这些假钞主要由浪人制造和流通。
2月15日，冀察政务委员会通知天津市政府，今后任何因伪造钞票被捕的人将被处决，以儆效尤。

February 15, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers:-

LABOUR TROUBLE AT THE KUNG YIH COTTON MILL.

The Kung Yih ( 公 益 ) otherwise Known as the
Ewo) Cotton Mill, Robinson Road, employs about 3,000 workers.
Yesterday the management posted up a notice
to the effect that the labour contract system is to be
abolished and that some 300 workers including seven foremen
will be discharged.
The workers demanded that they each be given
a retiring gratuity equivalent to six months' pay. The
negotiations had no result.
The workers subsequently held a meeting at
which representatives to submit an appeal to the local Tangou
and other government organs to-day to effect their reinstatement
were appointed.

1937年2月15日。下午译文。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：

公益纱厂的劳资纠纷。

公益 ( Kung Yih )（又称怡和 Ewo）纱厂，位于罗宾逊路，雇佣约3,000名工人。
昨天，管理层张贴公告，称将废除包身工制度，并将解雇包括七名工头在内的约300名工人。
工人要求每人获得相当于六个月工资的遣散费。谈判没有结果。
随后，工人举行会议，推选代表今天向当地党部 (Tangou) 和其他政府机构提交请愿书，以实现复职。
